Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="Challenger-PLAN005" color="purple" summary="PLAN-005 vector-challenger verdict: FAIL, 4 blocking issue classes">
vector-challenger review of PLAN-005 (plan@1, 28 tasks) against SPEC-005 (19 criteria). VERDICT: **FAIL** — 4 blocking issue classes.

All findings below were produced by actually executing the plan's steps against copies of the real files in an isolated /tmp fixture crate. The real repo files were never modified.

## What I spot-checked (empirically, not by reading prose)

1. **spec_hash — MATCH.** Plan declares `sha256:f40e54aab045c27d07a588ae6475f161e6001199ffc1724c2adcb89844c3c7a1`; `shasum -a 256 .claude/specs/SPEC-005.json` returns exactly that.

2. **On-disk assumption — TRUE.** types.rs is 91 lines, tests_types.rs is 241 lines with 17 tests, and both end `}\n\n` (od -c confirmed), exactly as the plan's reasoning claims.

3. **Append-only claim — TRUE, verified mechanically task-by-task.** Across all 28 tasks: 0 occurrences of `cat > <realfile>`, 28 of `cat >> <realfile>` (exactly one per task), 1 scoped `sed -i` (T-005's Utf8PathBuf import — I ran it; the `head -8 | tail -2` check passes). SPEC-003's committed content is never at risk. This claim holds.

4. **Fixture builds — real, and they work.** Built the described crate (edition 2024, serde/serde_json/camino, `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"`), copied the real files in, ran `cargo test`: 17 baseline tests pass, exit 0. Then executed the plan's appends. **All 11 intermediate types.rs snapshots compile with 0 errors** (T-001,003,005,009,011,013,015,017,019,021,023) — the topological ordering claim is proven, not merely asserted. With all 21 new tests appended and imports deduped: **38 passed, 0 failed** — the plan's test-count arithmetic (17→38) is exact at every task, and every behavioral serde claim holds (internal-tag snake_case field preservation, adjacent-tag 2-key shape, Selff→"self", Extern→`{"extern":"foo"}`, NamespaceWide→"namespaceWide", Vec default leniency, TsData selective skip, and every asserted error substring).

5. **T-023 / T-028 shared_file_note — PASS on substance.** Both do carry the fullest point-of-last-contact restatement (T-023 for types.rs, T-028 for tests_types.rs with the 38-test tally). One factual nit: both cite "PLAN-003's T-006/T-011 precedent," but PLAN-003 has exactly one shared_file_note, on T-006. T-011 carries none. PLAN-005 is establishing that precedent for tests_types.rs, not matching it.

6. **AC-019 representative sample — IT IS A REAL COVERAGE GAP, and it hides a spec defect.** Details in issue #4 below.

## Blocking issues

**#1 — T-006, T-007, T-008, T-024, T-025, T-026, T-027, T-028 · type: wrong-order · CRITICAL**
Each test task appends its own `use crate::types::...`, and 8 tasks re-import a name an earlier task already imported into the same module → `error[E0252]`. VERIFIED: appending T-002, T-004, then T-006 verbatim gives `error[E0252]: the name RustPathAnchor is defined multiple times --> src/tests_types.rs:286:38`, exit=101. T-006's own step 4 claims "20 passed" — it never compiles. Collisions: T-006 re-imports RustPathAnchor; T-007 and T-008 each re-import DependencyTarget; T-024 re-imports TsData; T-025 re-imports all 6; T-026 re-imports LangData; T-027 re-imports all 7; T-028 re-imports all 4. Everything from T-006 onward is blocked.
FIX: emit a `use` only for names not already imported. Corrected list (I ran the full suite with exactly these — 38 pass, exit 0): T-002 BindingKind; T-004 RustPathAnchor; T-006 DependencyTarget; T-007 none; T-008 none; T-010 DependencyBinding; T-012 DependencyRecord; T-014 ExportRecord; T-016 JsxAttribute; T-018 JsxElementEntry; T-020 {GoData, JavaData, PythonData, RustData}; T-022 TsData; T-024 LangData; T-025/026/027/028 none.

**#2 — T-001, T-003, T-009, T-011, T-013, T-015, T-017, T-021 · type: over-specified · CRITICAL**
Every scoped-block check is `grep -B<n> -A<m> '<anchor>' FILE | diff - <<'RUSTEOF' … RUSTEOF`. This cannot run: the heredoc claims diff's stdin so the pipe is discarded, leaving `diff -` with a single operand. VERIFIED: T-001's exact command prints diff's usage message, exit 2. The plan's primary structural verification fails on all 8 tasks regardless of file correctness — the same never-actually-executed-verification class that forced re-gate rounds on SPEC-001 and SPEC-003.
FIX: `diff <(grep -B<n> -A<m> '<anchor>' FILE) - <<'RUSTEOF' … RUSTEOF` (verified exit 0).

**#3 — same 8 tasks · type: over-specified · HIGH**
Independently, all 8 context windows are numerically wrong, so the comparison still fails after #2 is fixed. (a) Every `-A<m>` is one too large: each heredoc ends `}\n\n`, so grep captures a trailing blank the comparand lacks — T-001's `-B2 -A7` yields 10 lines vs a 9-line comparand (`10d9 < `), while `-A6` diffs clean. (b) T-011 `-B4` and T-021 `-B4` reach two lines into the doc comment; T-003's `grep -B6 -A7 … | tail -n +7` starts at `pub enum RustPathAnchor {`, dropping the three attribute lines the comparand opens with.
FIX (all confirmed to yield exactly the comparand, first line `#[derive(…)]`, last line `}`): T-001 `-B2 -A6`; T-003 `-B3 -A6` (drop `tail -n +7`); T-009 `-B2 -A4`; T-011 `-B2 -A5`; T-013 `-B2 -A4`; T-015 `-B2 -A5`; T-017 `-B2 -A5`; T-021 `-B2 -A7`.

**#4 — T-028 · type: missing-error-handling · HIGH**
AC-019's proof-by-representative-sample is a genuine gap that conceals a spec defect. AC-019 claims an extra unrecognized key "deserializes successfully for every one of these 14 types." T-028 samples ExportRecord (plain struct), RustData (fieldless), DependencyTarget (internal tag), LangData (adjacent tag) — and omits a fifth structurally distinct category in this very cluster: the **externally tagged** enum RustPathAnchor, whose `Extern(String)` is the only cluster member using serde's default enum strategy. VERIFIED: `from_str::<RustPathAnchor>(r#"{"extern":"foo","bogusKey":123}"#)` FAILS with `expected value at line 1 column 15`. **AC-019 is false as written.** Separately, BindingKind and RustPathAnchor's unit variants serialize as bare JSON strings, so "an object with an extra key" is inapplicable (`from_str::<BindingKind>(r#"{"named":null,"bogus":1}"#)` also errors). Of AC-019's 14 types: true for 12, false for RustPathAnchor, vacuous for BindingKind. The chosen sample is exactly the subset that stays green.
FIX: this needs a canon correction, not a plan patch. Route AC-019 to canon-drafter correction mode to narrow it to the 12 types whose wire form is a named-field JSON object, and add a criterion pinning that externally-tagged RustPathAnchor::Extern rejects extra keys. Then add a task asserting that. If the spec is left as-is, T-028 must at minimum add the RustPathAnchor case so it fails loudly via lambda-implementer's contradiction path rather than shipping a green suite that "proves" a false criterion.

**#5 — T-001 · over-specified · MEDIUM.** `grep -c 'No .#\[non_exhaustive\].'` expects 1, actual **2** — SymbolKind's pre-existing SPEC-003 doc at types.rs:12 matches the same pattern. False failure halts the implementer. FIX: `grep -c '^/// No .#\[non_exhaustive\].\.$'` → 1 (verified).

**#6 — T-003, T-005, T-021, T-023 · over-specified · MEDIUM.** Four more `grep -c` assertions expect 1 but return **2**, because each task's own doc comment quotes the attribute it counts. T-003 `#[serde(rename = "self")]` → 2; T-005 `tag = "kind"` → 2; T-021 `skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty"` → 2; T-023 `tag = "language", content = "data"` → 2. All four verified. FIX (all verified → 1): anchor to line start — `^    #\[serde(rename = "self")\]$`, `^#\[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "kind")\]$`, `^    #\[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")\]$`, `^#\[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", tag = "language", content = "data")\]$`.

## Non-blocking

**#7 — T-003 · under-specified · LOW.** Step 3 contains `grep -c 'would$' <file> | true;` — dead clause, exit status swallowed, no stated expectation. Looks like an editing leftover. FIX: delete it; the following grep returns 1 (verified).

**#8 — T-005, T-019, T-023 · under-specified · LOW.** These three replace the scoped diff with prose soft checks ("should show the 3 variants…", "should show the 5 variants…", and T-019's `grep -A26 … | head -1` which merely restates the anchor). Nothing pins field order or attribute text, so a transposed field passes. The exact-shape half of AC-005/AC-012/AC-018 rests on eyeballs. FIX: give all three the same corrected `diff <(grep …) -` treatment. The fixture cargo test proves behavior, not declaration order.

**#9 — T-004 · under-specified · LOW.** Step 3 offers two commands and lets the implementer pick ("if this exact escaping is ambiguous to grep, instead run… and rely on the fixture cargo test"). FIX: pick one — drop the brittle nested-quote grep and state that T-004's proof is the fixture's exact string equalities (they do hold: `"self"` and `{"extern":"foo"}`).

**#10 — T-006/T-007 · orphaned-criteria · LOW.** Mis-attribution, not a gap. AC-005 carries its own error clause ("isRelative" instead of "is_relative" → missing-field error). The test proving it, `dependency_target_camel_case_field_key_fails_missing_field`, lives in T-007 whose covers_criteria is `['AC-006']` only; T-006 (which covers AC-005) asserts serialization shape but not the deserialize failure. Behavior is tested and passes — the mapping just misdirects the exit gate's criteria_evidence trace. FIX: make T-007's covers_criteria `['AC-005','AC-006']`.

**#11 — shared_file_warning + T-028.shared_file_note · LOW.** False provenance claim, see spot-check 5 above. FIX: cite PLAN-003's T-006 as the types.rs precedent; state that T-028 extends the discipline to tests_types.rs for the first time.

## Dimension summary
- missing coverage: **none** — all 19 ACs appear in ≥1 covers_criteria
- orphaned criteria: **none** at ID level; one mis-attribution (#10)
- wrong order: type-dependency order correct and compile-verified; but 8 tasks fail to compile for a different ordering reason (#1, blocking)
- over-specified: 3 blocking clusters (#2, #3, #5/#6)
- under-specified: 4 low items (#7–#9, #11)
- too large: **none** — every task is one heredoc append + greps + one fixture cargo test, well under 15 min
- missing error handling: all 9 `is_error_case` criteria have test steps and all pass; but AC-019's sample omits the one category that falsifies it (#4, blocking)

## Bottom line
The plan's substance is sound — ordering, coverage, append-only discipline, and every serde behavioral claim survive real execution, and the 38-test end state is achievable exactly as specified. What fails is the verification scaffolding (the scoped diffs never ran; the import scheme doesn't compile) plus AC-019, which is empirically false for RustPathAnchor and needs a canon correction rather than a plan patch.

Files: plan `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/plans/PLAN-005.json`; spec `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/specs/SPEC-005.json`; targets `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/types.rs` and `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/tests_types.rs` (both unmodified).
</teammate-message>

**#2 — T-001, T-003, T-009, T-011, T-013, T-015, T-017, T-021 · type: over-specified · CRITICAL**

  "purpose": "Define the complete, compilable, verbatim shape and observable serde contract of monokl's dependency/export/JSX/language-data type cluster -- DependencyRecord, DependencyBinding, BindingKind, DependencyTarget, RustPathAnchor, ExportRecord, JsxAttribute, JsxElementEntry, LangData (plus its two methods), and the five per-language data structs (TsData, RustData, PythonData, GoData, JavaData) -- per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 4 (lines 312-452), so a developer implementing types.rs, or any downstream analyzer constructing these values, never has to guess a variant, field, serde tag strategy, or rename. This cluster is where two structurally different serde enum-tagging strategies coexist (DependencyTarget's internally-tagged `tag = \"kind\"`, which flattens each variant's fields into the same JSON object as the tag, versus LangData's adjacently-tagged `tag = \"language\", content = \"data\"`, which keeps the tag and the variant's payload in two separate keys) and where some #[serde(rename = ...)] overrides are functionally necessary to produce the intended JSON string (RustPathAnchor::Selff -> \"self\"; LangData::Ts -> \"typescript\") while others are redundant with what the enclosing rename_all = \"camelCase\" would already produce on its own -- precision an implementer would otherwise have to reverse-engineer from serde's own transform rules rather than read directly.",
  "scope": "DependencyRecord (3 fields), DependencyBinding (3 fields), BindingKind (5 variants), DependencyTarget (an internally-tagged, #[non_exhaustive] 3-variant enum), RustPathAnchor (a #[non_exhaustive] 4-variant enum with one functionally necessary rename), ExportRecord (3 fields), JsxAttribute (4 fields), JsxElementEntry (4 fields), LangData (an adjacently-tagged, #[non_exhaustive] 5-variant enum plus its ts()/jsx_elements() methods), TsData (3 fields, the only one of the five per-language data structs with real content), and RustData/PythonData/GoData/JavaData (four structurally identical empty placeholder structs) -- all verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:312-452, including the \"Post-research correction\" note at lines 397-400 explaining why Go/Java replace an earlier CSharp variant. docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md independently restates RustPathAnchor (03-multi-language-platform.md:2405-2417), DependencyTarget (2419-2442), and LangData plus its ts()/jsx_elements() methods (2381-2403) in its own 'types added' changelog block, each confirmed semantically identical to the canonical source -- differing only in single-line-vs-multi-line attribute formatting, no drift found. It locks each type's exact field/variant order, derive list, and serde attributes; the two distinct enum-tagging JSON shapes these types produce; which #[serde(rename = ...)] overrides are necessary versus redundant; and the observable deserialize consequences of #[non_exhaustive] (a Rust-level match-exhaustiveness attribute with no effect on serde's generated (de)serialize code) versus the presence or absence of #[serde(default)] on Vec-typed fields, which -- unlike Option-typed fields -- do not get implicit missing-key leniency from serde's derive macro without that attribute.",

Another Claude session sent a message:
<teammate-message teammate_id="Challenger-PLAN005-v2" color="green" summary="PLAN-005 v2 re-review: FAIL, 3 blocking defects">
vector-challenger re-review of AMENDED PLAN-005 (29 tasks) vs SPEC-005 (21 ACs). VERDICT: **fail** — 3 blocking defects survive the amendment. 8 of the 10 claimed fixes are genuine; 2 (claims #3 and #5) were applied to every task except T-002.

## WHAT I ACTUALLY EXECUTED

Read PLAN-005.json and SPEC-005.json fresh from disk. Built an isolated fixture crate (edition 2024, serde + serde_json + camino/serde1, `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"`, rustc/cargo 1.96.0) and ran **all 29 tasks' append/sed + verify + fixture-test steps in sequence** against copies of the real `crates/monokl/src/{types.rs,tests_types.rs}`. Only the file path was substituted; every command otherwise verbatim. **The real repo files were never modified — `git status --short crates/monokl/src/` is empty.**

Result: the full run compiles clean at every step (zero E0252, zero errors, zero warnings) and reaches **exactly 40 tests**, matching the plan's claim. Every single intermediate count the plan states reproduced exactly: 17,18,18,19,19,20,23,24,24,25,25,26,26,27,27,28,28,29,29,30,30,31,31,32,33,36,37,38,40.

Additionally executed: mutation tests against the scoped diffs and against T-029; a clippy run under the workspace's own lint table; a probe binary exercising every AC-004B/AC-019B input shape; a `preserve_order` parity run; jq sweeps over PLAN-003.json and PLAN-005.json.

## THE 10 CLAIMED FIXES, RE-VERIFIED

1. **AC-019 narrowed / AC-004B+AC-019B added / T-029 added — CONFIRMED.** Spec on disk has 21 ACs. T-029 exists, `depends_on: ["T-028"]`, `covers_criteria: ["AC-004B","AC-019B"]`. `spec_hash` in the plan matches `shasum -a 256` of the spec byte-for-byte.
2. **Import collisions — CONFIRMED.** Full run: zero E0252. Import ledger is disjoint (T-002 BindingKind, T-004 RustPathAnchor, T-006 DependencyTarget, T-010 DependencyBinding, T-012 DependencyRecord, T-014 ExportRecord, T-016 JsxAttribute, T-018 JsxElementEntry, T-020 the four empty structs, T-022 TsData, T-024 LangData). T-007/008/025/026/027/028/029 correctly add no `use` line. No unused-import warnings either.
3. **`grep | diff -` → `diff <(grep ...) -` — PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. T-002 STILL BROKEN.** 11 tasks now use process substitution and all 11 exited 0. But a jq sweep of every step shows T-002 still carries `grep -A16 ... | diff - <<'RUSTEOF'`, which reproduced the original failure live: diff printed its usage block and exited 2.
4. **-B/-A windows — CONFIRMED.** All 11 diffs exited 0 with *empty* output, i.e. each window captured exactly the heredoc and nothing more.
5. **False-failure `grep -c` — PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. T-002 STILL FALSE-FAILS.** Every grep in T-001/003/005/021/023 returned its stated value. I ran all 60+ grep -c assertions plan-wide at their own task's point in time; all matched **except T-002's**, which returns 0 where 1 is expected.
6. **T-003's dead `grep -c 'would$' | true;` — CONFIRMED removed.**
7. **T-005/T-019/T-023 upgraded to real scoped diffs — CONFIRMED** (-B3-A16 / -B4-A18 / -B3-A11, all exit 0). T-005's new `head -8 | tail -2` import-position check also prints the right two lines.
8. **T-004 simplified — CONFIRMED.** Now a single grep plus prose deferring to cargo test.
9. **T-007 covers_criteria — CONFIRMED and correct on the merits.** Its three tests genuinely map to AC-005 + AC-006. Sweep found one remaining lower-severity mis-attribution (issue #5 below).
10. **shared_file_note provenance — CONFIRMED.** jq: T-028 has none, T-029 does. jq over PLAN-003.json confirms exactly one task there carries a shared_file_note (T-006), so "per that plan's established precedent (its T-006)" is now accurate.

## ARE THE CHECKS REAL? (non-vacuousness)

Diffs: mutated three things and each was caught — reordered BindingKind variants → exit 1; dropped Copy/PartialEq/Eq from BindingKind's derive → exit 1; dropped `skip_serializing_if` from `TsData.unresolved_aliases` → exit 1.

**T-029 specifically:** gave BindingKind `tag = "k"` → `binding_kind_external_tagging_shapes` FAILED (3 failures total); renamed `NamespaceWide`'s wire form to `"namespace_wide"` → FAILED; gave RustPathAnchor `tag="t", content="c"` → `rust_path_anchor_unknown_variant_and_second_key_rejected` FAILED. Restoring correct declarations → 40/40 green. T-029 is not vacuous.

**Spec accuracy:** every AC-004B/AC-019B claim reproduces byte-for-byte, including the column offsets the spec's revision_note cites — `{"named":null,"bogusKey":1}` → `expected value at line 1 column 13`; `{"extern":"foo","bogusKey":123}` → `column 15`; `123`/`true`/`null`/`["named"]` → `column 1`; all five `expected unit` invalid-type errors; the full `expected one of ...` variant list. T-029's content is consistent with the corrected spec text.

**Coverage:** union of all covers_criteria == the spec's AC set exactly (21/21), no phantom IDs, no orphans. `depends_on` is a single strict chain T-001 → … → T-029.

## ISSUES

**#1 — T-005 · under-specified · BLOCKING**
`sed -i.bak '/^use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};$/i use camino::Utf8PathBuf;' … && rm ….bak` is GNU-only. On this darwin machine BSD sed rejects the one-line `i text` form: `sed: 1: "/^use serde::{Deseriali ...": command i expects \ followed by text`, exit 1, no insertion. The append half of step 3 is a separate command and still runs, so types.rs ends up with DependencyTarget referencing `Utf8PathBuf` with no import — T-005's own `grep -c '^use camino::Utf8PathBuf;$'` returns 0 (expects 1) and its fixture test fails to compile. **T-006 through T-029 are all blocked.** Not among the 10 claimed fixes; T-005's sed is unchanged. The plan's `reasoning` field also asserts this edit is made "via a scoped sed insertion" as settled fact.
*Fix (verified working here — exit 0, grep→1, `head -8|tail -2` correct, no stray .bak):*
`perl -i -pe 's{^use serde::\{Deserialize, Serialize\};$}{use camino::Utf8PathBuf;\nuse serde::\{Deserialize, Serialize\};}' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/types.rs`
Drop the `&& rm ….bak` clause. Keep both existing verification checks — they already discriminate success from failure correctly. Add a caution that the substitution is not idempotent (a second run duplicates the import).

**#2 — T-002 · under-specified · BLOCKING**
The scoped block check fails three independent ways. (a) Still `grep -A16 … | diff - <<'RUSTEOF'` — the heredoc redirects diff's stdin so `-` consumes it and the pipe is discarded, leaving diff one operand; executed verbatim it printed its usage block and exited 2, so the check can never pass *or* meaningfully fail. (b) The comparand is knowingly wrong — plain words `(BindingKind::Named, "named")` vs the file's `(BindingKind::Named, "\"named\"")`. (c) The window is off by one: -A16 spans 17 lines against a 15-line comparand. (d) The step then says "run the check against the real file's literal bytes … if the escaping renders ambiguously", handing the implementer the job of inventing the comparand — a design decision the plan should already have made. Note T-004's step states the principle "this plan does not attempt brittle nested-quote grepping"; T-002 violates it.
*Fix (verified: exit 0 on correct content; exit 1 when I corrupted `\"glob\"` → `\"Glob\"`):* use `diff <(grep -B1 -A14 '^fn binding_kind_camel_case_forms() {$' …) - <<'RUSTEOF'` with the comparand as the file's **literal bytes** (backslash-escaped quotes), first line `#[test]`. Delete the "if the escaping renders ambiguously" sentence.

**#3 — T-002 · under-specified · BLOCKING**
`grep -c 'NamespaceWide, "\"namespaceWide\""'` expecting 1. In single quotes the shell passes `\"` through; grep BRE then treats `\"` as plain `"`, so the effective pattern is `NamespaceWide, ""namespaceWide""`, which cannot match the file's `NamespaceWide, "\"namespaceWide\""`. Run against the real post-append file: **returns 0**. Same defect class as claimed fix #5, applied everywhere but here.
*Fix (verified → 1):* `grep -cF 'NamespaceWide, "\"namespaceWide\""' …` (BRE alternative `grep -c 'NamespaceWide, "\\"namespaceWide\\""'` also returns 1, but -F is clearer). Or drop it — the corrected diff in #2 already pins that line.

**#4 — T-029 · missing-error-handling · non-blocking**
T-029 proves AC-004B parts (a), (b), (c), one representative of (d), and (e)(i). Untested: **(e)(ii)** — `from_str::<BindingKind>("123")`, `("true")`, `("null")`, `(r#"["named"]"#)`. That sub-case is exactly what the spec's second correction pass existed to fix (the fifth draft mis-stated it as a type-mismatch error), so the corrected claim is unguarded by any test. Also unproven: (b)'s "naming all 5 recognized forms" (only `contains("unknown variant")`), and (d)'s other four payload kinds. **Non-blocking** because I verified empirically that (e)(ii) and (d)'s extra kinds are serde_json *parser-level* properties invariant to any plausible change to BindingKind's declaration, and (b)'s variant list is already pinned exactly by T-002's 5-variant round-trip.
*Fix:* add after the `err3` block — `for bad in ["123", "true", "null", r#"["named"]"#] { let e = serde_json::from_str::<BindingKind>(bad).unwrap_err(); assert!(e.to_string().contains("expected value")); }` — and strengthen (b) to assert the full ``expected one of `named`, `default`, `namespace`, `glob`, `namespaceWide` `` string (reproduces verbatim). Bump the task's `grep -c 'contains("expected value")'` expectation 2 → 3.

**#5 — T-004 · missing-coverage · non-blocking**
Same class as the T-007 mis-attribution that claim #9 fixed. AC-019B has a serialize half (Crate/Super/Selff → bare strings; `Extern` → `{"extern":"foo"}`) and a rejection half. T-004's test proves the serialize half exactly — all four literal wire forms — but lists only `["AC-008"]`. T-029, the only task claiming AC-019B, tests only the rejection half. Not orphaned, but an exit gate reading covers_criteria would conclude AC-019B's serialize half is unproven.
*Fix:* set T-004's covers_criteria to `["AC-008","AC-019B"]`. No test change needed.

**#6 — T-005/T-013/T-015/T-019/T-021/T-023 · quality · non-blocking**
Ran clippy with the workspace's own lint table (pedantic=warn + the unwrap/expect/panic denies + the four allows). SPEC-003's committed types.rs alone: **0** `doc_markdown` warnings. After all 29 tasks: **21**, every one in a new SPEC-005 doc comment — types.rs:137,149 (T-005), :207 (T-013), :218,221 (T-015), :259,265 (T-019), :273-275 (T-021), :287,290,291,300 (T-023). Inconsistent within the plan itself: T-001/003/009/011 backtick their identifiers and warn zero times. Non-blocking — pedantic is warn-level, there's no CI workflow or `-D warnings` gate in this repo, and AGENTS.md's only clippy requirement is the unwrap/expect/panic denies.
*Fix:* backtick the flagged identifiers. **Constraint:** three of the plan's own grep anchors live in these comments and must survive verbatim — T-005's `'not isRelative/isStatic'` and `'finding #20'`, T-019's `'replaces the dropped'`, T-023's `'only Ts.s rename to "typescript" is'`. None is among the flagged spans. Update the affected scoped-diff heredocs to match the new bytes.

**#7 — T-020 · quality · non-blocking**
`fn assert_default<T: Default>() {}` declared after statements → `clippy::items_after_statements` at tests_types.rs:466. SPEC-003's analogous `field_types_and_derives_pinned` puts its helpers at the top of the body and warns zero times.
*Fix:* move it to the first line of the test body. No assertion changes.

**#8 — plan.reasoning · stale amendment text · non-blocking**
Two counts not updated when AC-019 went 14 → 12 types: "spanning all **three** serde-shape categories" then enumerates four (and the spec's own revision_note says "4 distinct serde-shape categories"); and "rather than writing all **14** as separate assertions", contradicting the same sentence's later "12 times". Documentation-only. Also: `architecture`'s "Behavioral test tasks interleave immediately after each structural task" no longer describes T-029, appended at the end.
*Fix:* three → four; 14 → 12; add a half-sentence noting T-029 as the amendment's deliberate exception (depends on T-028 only so the 38→40 arithmetic stays sequential; its subjects exist from T-001/T-003, so no dependency is violated).

## FIDELITY NOTE (not an issue)
The plan's fixture omits serde_json's `preserve_order`, which the real workspace pins. I re-ran the final 40 tests with it enabled — still 40/40 green, so the omission is behaviorally inert here.

## FILES
Plan `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/plans/PLAN-005.json`; spec `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/specs/SPEC-005.json`; harness + full transcripts under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl/a82f4f80-7822-4785-a872-33c66baeee45/scratchpad/` (`setup.sh`, `run1.sh`–`run4.sh`, `mutate.sh`, `vc2/`).

**overall: fail.** Fixing #1, #2, #3 clears the blocking set; #4 and #5 are cheap and worth folding into the same pass before the 29 lambda dispatches begin.
</teammate-message>

7. **T-005/T-019/T-023 upgraded to real scoped diffs — CONFIRMED** (-B3-A16 / -B4-A18 / -B3-A11, all exit 0). T-005's new `head -8 | tail -2` import-position check also prints the right two lines.

Diffs: mutated three things and each was caught — reordered BindingKind variants → exit 1; dropped Copy/PartialEq/Eq from BindingKind's derive → exit 1; dropped `skip_serializing_if` from `TsData.unresolved_aliases` → exit 1.

**T-029 specifically:** gave BindingKind `tag = "k"` → `binding_kind_external_tagging_shapes` FAILED (3 failures total); renamed `NamespaceWide`'s wire form to `"namespace_wide"` → FAILED; gave RustPathAnchor `tag="t", content="c"` → `rust_path_anchor_unknown_variant_and_second_key_rejected` FAILED. Restoring correct declarations → 40/40 green. T-029 is not vacuous.

**Spec accuracy:** every AC-004B/AC-019B claim reproduces byte-for-byte, including the column offsets the spec's revision_note cites — `{"named":null,"bogusKey":1}` → `expected value at line 1 column 13`; `{"extern":"foo","bogusKey":123}` → `column 15`; `123`/`true`/`null`/`["named"]` → `column 1`; all five `expected unit` invalid-type errors; the full `expected one of ...` variant list. T-029's content is consistent with the corrected spec text.

**Coverage:** union of all covers_criteria == the spec's AC set exactly (21/21), no phantom IDs, no orphans. `depends_on` is a single strict chain T-001 → … → T-029.

**#1 — T-005 · under-specified · BLOCKING**
`sed -i.bak '/^use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};$/i use camino::Utf8PathBuf;' … && rm ….bak` is GNU-only. On this darwin machine BSD sed rejects the one-line `i text` form: `sed: 1: "/^use serde::{Deseriali ...": command i expects \ followed by text`, exit 1, no insertion. The append half of step 3 is a separate command and still runs, so types.rs ends up with DependencyTarget referencing `Utf8PathBuf` with no import — T-005's own `grep -c '^use camino::Utf8PathBuf;$'` returns 0 (expects 1) and its fixture test fails to compile. **T-006 through T-029 are all blocked.** Not among the 10 claimed fixes; T-005's sed is unchanged. *Fix (verified working here — exit 0, grep→1, `head -8|tail -2` correct, no stray .bak):*
`perl -i -pe 's{^use serde::\{Deserialize, Serialize\};$}{use camino::Utf8PathBuf;\nuse serde::\{Deserialize, Serialize\};}' /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/types.rs`

**#2 — T-002 · under-specified · BLOCKING**
The scoped block check fails three independent ways. (a) Still `grep -A16 … | diff - <<'RUSTEOF'` — the heredoc redirects diff's stdin so `-` consumes it and the pipe is discarded, leaving diff one operand; executed verbatim it printed its usage block and exited 2, so the check can never pass *or* meaningfully fail. (b) The comparand is knowingly wrong — plain words `(BindingKind::Named, "named")` vs the file's `(BindingKind::Named, "\"named\"")`. (c) The window is off by one: -A16 spans 17 lines against a 15-line comparand. (d) The step then says "run the check against the real file's literal bytes … if the escaping renders ambiguously", handing the implementer the job of inventing the comparand — a design decision the plan should already have made. Note T-004's step states the principle "this plan does not attempt brittle nested-quote grepping"; T-002 violates it.
*Fix (verified: exit 0 on correct content; exit 1 when I corrupted `\"glob\"` → `\"Glob\"`):* use `diff <(grep -B1 -A14 '^fn binding_kind_camel_case_forms() {$' …) - <<'RUSTEOF'` with the comparand as the file's **literal bytes** (backslash-escaped quotes), first line `#[test]`. Delete the "if the escaping renders ambiguously" sentence.

**#3 — T-002 · under-specified · BLOCKING**
`grep -c 'NamespaceWide, "\"namespaceWide\""'` expecting 1. In single quotes the shell passes `\"` through; grep BRE then treats `\"` as plain `"`, so the effective pattern is `NamespaceWide, ""namespaceWide""`, which cannot match the file's `NamespaceWide, "\"namespaceWide\""`. Run against the real post-append file: **returns 0**. Same defect class as claimed fix #5, applied everywhere but here.
*Fix (verified → 1):* `grep -cF 'NamespaceWide, "\"namespaceWide\""' …` (BRE alternative `grep -c 'NamespaceWide, "\\"namespaceWide\\""'` also returns 1, but -F is clearer). Or drop it — the corrected diff in #2 already pins that line.

**#4 — T-029 · missing-error-handling · non-blocking**
T-029 proves AC-004B parts (a), (b), (c), one representative of (d), and (e)(i). Untested: **(e)(ii)** — `from_str::<BindingKind>("123")`, `("true")`, `("null")`, `(r#"["named"]"#)`. That sub-case is exactly what the spec's second correction pass existed to fix (the fifth draft mis-stated it as a type-mismatch error), so the corrected claim is unguarded by any test. Also unproven: (b)'s "naming all 5 recognized forms" (only `contains("unknown variant")`), and (d)'s other four payload kinds. **Non-blocking** because I verified empirically that (e)(ii) and (d)'s extra kinds are serde_json *parser-level* properties invariant to any plausible change to BindingKind's declaration, and (b)'s variant list is already pinned exactly by T-002's 5-variant round-trip.

Bump the task's `grep -c 'contains("expected value")'` expectation 2 → 3.

Same class as the T-007 mis-attribution that claim #9 fixed. AC-019B has a serialize half (Crate/Super/Selff → bare strings; `Extern` → `{"extern":"foo"}`) and a rejection half. T-004's test proves the serialize half exactly — all four literal wire forms — but lists only `["AC-008"]`. T-029, the only task claiming AC-019B, tests only the rejection half. payload.message:
We're not touching michi yet — no dependency exists in either `Cargo.toml` currently, and nothing in `crates/monokl/src/` references it.

It's entirely scoped to **SPEC-010** ("michi output/error adapter"), which specifies both the exact dependency declaration (`github.com/orin-axi/michi`, AGPL-3.0-or-later) and the trait/adapter design that converts monokl's own domain types — `MonoklError` (SPEC-001), `CodeBlock`/`RankedBlock` (SPEC-006), `SearchResponse`/`SymbolsResult`/`DependentsResult` (SPEC-007) — into michi's rendering types (`DomainError`, `AgentResponse`, `Value`) at one narrow boundary.

That's why SPEC-010 is deliberately last in the implementation sequence (SPEC-001 → 003 → 005 → 006 → 007 → 008 → 009 → 010): it needs those source types to exist as real, gated code first, not just as spec text. SPEC-001 is done; SPEC-005 is finishing up now (fix round 4 in flight); SPEC-006/007/008/009 are still ahead. Once those land, SPEC-010 wires in michi for real.

Real `cargo test`: 57 passed, 0 failed.
4. Independently re-applied every mutation pass 3 and fix round 4 described. All 10 killed:
   - (a) File.specifier +serde(default) → killed
   - (b) RustPath.segments / Namespace.segments / Namespace.is_static +serde(default), each individually → all killed
   - (c) RustPath omitting `resolved` deserializes to None → confirmed live at tests_types.rs:350-352
   - (d) JsxElementEntry.name / is_html / line +serde(default), each individually → all killed
   - (e) DependencyRecord.line / ExportRecord.line / JsxElementEntry.line → i64, each individually → all killed as GENUINE COMPILE ERRORS (E0308 at tests_types.rs:885, `let dep_line: usize = dep.line;`), not runtime-assertion catches. Fix round 4's claim verified true.
5. Fresh broad adversarial sweep: 125 mutations total across three rounds — attribute add/remove, tag strategy changes, rename changes, field type swaps, field order swaps, variant order swaps, extra variant/field additions, derive removals, deny_unknown_fields on all 12 AC-019 types, and method-body mutations. 116 killed, 9 equivalent/unobservable, 5 real gaps (above).

7. Commit range 21dce1e..d716afa touched ONLY crates/monokl/src/types.rs and crates/monokl/src/tests_types.rs. error.rs (SPEC-001) is untouched — zero commits against it in the range.
8. Mutation testing (lambda-mutator) on record from prior passes, confirmed.

DELIBERATELY NOT RAISED AS BLOCKERS
- #[non_exhaustive] presence/absence (AC-003/005/008/012): all four mutations survive, but the attribute is a no-op intra-crate and the spec itself states it has zero serde effect. Not reachable without a downstream crate.
- rename_all removal on DependencyRecord/DependencyBinding: equivalent mutants — every field name is a single lowercase word.
- LangData::Rust redundant rename removal: survives, which is exactly what AC-013 predicts.
- Field visibility pub → pub(crate): not observable from in-crate tests.

THE META-FINDING — this is the part I'd flag for the human

B-1, B-2 and B-3 are not new classes. They are unswept members of classes passes 2 and 3 already named. Pass 3 listed 4 DependencyTarget required fields; there are 6. Pass 3 pinned `line: usize`; the sibling field type in the same criterion went unpinned. Each round has closed the enumerated instances rather than the class, which is why a 4th pass still finds items — and why a 5th targeted instance-list round would likely repeat the pattern.

RECOMMENDATION (human's call)

Rather than another instance list, one of two things:
(a) Adopt a systematic mutation sweep as the acceptance bar. My harness is at .../scratchpad/sweep.py with the fixture at .../scratchpad/fx/ — runs in ~90 seconds and would have caught all five in one shot. It ran entirely against a copied fixture; nothing touched the repo.
(b) Accept these five as documented debt. Defensible: the implementation itself has been confirmed correct across four independent passes, and B-4/B-5 are medium/low severity.

I would not recommend a 5th targeted fix round on these five specific items alone without also sweeping their classes, since that is the pattern that produced this pass.

<teammate-message teammate_id="Challenger-PLAN006" color="blue" summary="PLAN-006 review: FAIL, 2 blocking error-case gaps">
vector-challenger review of PLAN-006 (plan@1, 21 tasks) against SPEC-006 (15 ACs). Verdict: FAIL — 2 blocking-class issues. Both fixes independently verified passing.

Bottom line first: the plan author's empirical-rigor claim GENUINELY HOLDS. I re-executed it rather than trusting it, and every quantitative claim reproduced. The field-type-pinning defect class that cost PLAN-005 six gate cycles is genuinely closed. The two blockers I found are a DIFFERENT class, described below.

=== WHAT I ACTUALLY EXECUTED ===

1. Full 21-task fixture run. Built my own isolated crate (edition 2024, bare [workspace], serde/serde_json/camino, [lints.rust] unsafe_code="deny"), copied pristine crates/monokl/src/{types.rs,tests_types.rs} (337 / 1296 lines, 62 tests baseline), programmatically extracted each task's `cat >>` heredoc from the plan JSON, applied all 21 in order, ran cargo test after every one.
   RESULT: exactly 79 passed, 0 failed, 0 rustc warnings. All 21 intermediate counts matched the plan exactly: 62,62,63,65,67,68,68,69,69,70,71,72,72,73,74,74,75,76,77,77,78,79.

2. preserve_order divergence test. The real workspace pins serde_json with feature preserve_order; the plan's fixture manifest uses bare serde_json="1". Since preserve_order swaps serde_json::Map from BTreeMap to IndexMap, and RankedBlock's flatten forces a map serialization path, I re-ran the entire 21-task sequence under the real feature set. Byte-identical results — 79/0/0. The mismatch is benign here, but the plan proves nothing about that either way.

3. Field-type-pinning inventory cross-check (the priority item). I parsed the post-simulation types.rs and built my OWN field inventory rather than reading T-021's claims: CodeBlock 8, ParentContext 3, RankedBlock 7, Diagnostic 3 = 21 fields. Cross-checked every one against T-021's body. All 21 have a genuine compile-time `let pinned_x: ExactType = field;` binding, each behind an exhaustive destructure with NO `..` rest pattern (so a future 9th field fails to compile). This is NOT a sample. The claim holds.

4. Stress tests requested:
   - flatten (AC-006): T-009 is not a tautology. It hardcodes the two key sets and calls BTreeSet::is_disjoint, but then GROUNDS them against reality via assert_eq!(actual_keys, expected_keys) and obj.len()==14, so an introduced collision fails the test. Verified no "block" wrapper key.
   - NaN/Infinity (AC-008): confirmed by EXECUTION, not assumption. serde_json really does emit null for non-finite f64. T-011 covers all 4 scoring fields x 3 non-finite values = 12 combinations, exceeding the spec.
   - rename_all="lowercase" (AC-012/013): read docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md:498-504 directly. The source says "lowercase". INTENTIONAL, correctly transcribed, NOT a plan error. All 6 declarations match the source doc verbatim.
   - Diagnostic no-source-field (AC-011): T-017's `..`-free destructure is a genuine compile-time proof of exactly 3 fields.
   - T-017 anchor sequence-order landmine: GENUINELY HANDLED. I ran all 58 grep anchors against my assembled final file — 57 matched exactly. The single mismatch is T-017's (expects 1, final file has 2 because T-021 adds a textually identical line). I re-simulated to T-017's own point: count is exactly 1 there. The step text explicitly documents this as a same-task immediately-after-append check with the reason. Not a landmine.

5. Clippy delta (plan never runs it). Replicated the real workspace lint config: 69 warnings baseline -> 115 after. New categories: 4x float_cmp, 1x unreadable_literal. All warn-level, baseline already 69. Non-blocking.

6. spec_hash sha256:4ce748ef0557accc4bc5e5c3dea6cfdb42787d3eb1eee55745a21fbe7a73b73a — matches raw SPEC-006.json sha256 exactly.

7. Coverage/order: all 15 ACs in some covers_criteria, zero orphans, zero missing. Dependency order CodeBlock->ParentContext->RankedBlock->DiagnosticKind->Diagnostic->LineHit is correct and every intermediate state compiles standalone (proven by cargo test after each task). All 6 `use crate::types::X;` lines appear exactly once. No task exceeds ~15 min.

=== ISSUES ===

[BLOCKING] task_id T-016 | type: missing-error-handling
DESCRIPTION: AC-010 (is_error_case: true) explicitly states Diagnostic carries no deny_unknown_fields and that an object with an extra key beyond kind/path/message deserializes successfully, silently discarding it. NO task tests this. I grepped every Diagnostic JSON literal in T-016/T-017/T-018 — all contain only kind/path/message. CodeBlock's identical sub-clause IS tested (T-004, "extraField"), and SPEC-005 tested its equivalent ("bogusKey":123 at tests_types.rs:610). So this is an inconsistency with established project practice, not a deliberate omission.

The other real lever, which is a tradeoff I shouldn't make unilaterally: I can dial back how many gate rounds we chase before accepting a pass — e.g., stop after 1 round of fixes and accept remaining non-blocking items as documented debt, rather than pushing for the full adversarial-mutation-sweep-verified ideal every time. That would cut gate rounds further but means somewhat less certainty in the final code.

Want me to set that lower bar going forward (accept after 1 fix round, log the rest as debt) for SPEC-007 onward?

The lever that actually moved the needle already: SPEC-006 took 2 gate rounds instead of SPEC-005's 6, purely because I front-loaded SPEC-005's lessons into the plan before review started. I'm doing the same for SPEC-007 right now. That's probably worth another 2-3x speedup as it compounds across specs.

The other real lever, which is a tradeoff I shouldn't make unilaterally: I can dial back how many gate rounds we chase before accepting a pass — e.g., stop after 1 round of fixes and accept remaining non-blocking items as documented debt, rather than pushing for the full adversarial-mutation-sweep-verified ideal every time. That would cut gate rounds further but means somewhat less certainty in the final code.

Want me to set that lower bar going forward (accept after 1 fix round, log the rest as debt) for SPEC-007 onward?

1. spec_hash verification. sha256 of the RAW bytes of .claude/specs/SPEC-007.json == 09f6159c31f1c939f5f1af82af654b6142d41e9b0e7a1ad381932ee12e863a19, exactly the plan's claimed spec_hash. Match.

2. Full 27-task re-execution in my own isolated fixture. Built a fresh crate (edition 2024, serde/serde_json+preserve_order/camino+serde1/clap 4 +derive+env behind an optional `cli` feature, default=["cli"] mirroring the real crate's default=["lang-ts","cli"]). clap IS genuinely needed — Language's clap::ValueEnum derive is cfg_attr-gated on `cli`. The 115/114 claim is confirmed.

3. FIELD TYPE PINNING (the PLAN-005 defect class) — verified exhaustively, not by sample. I built my OWN field inventory by reading the post-simulation types.rs declarations directly: SearchLimits 4, SearchOptions 7, SearchResponse 7, SymbolsResult 4, DependentsResult 7 = 29 fields. I then cross-checked EVERY ONE against T-027. All 29/29 have a genuine typed binding (`let pinned_*: ConcreteType = field;`). Field lists and order match AC-001/AC-004/AC-011/AC-013/AC-015 verbatim; derive lists match AC-001/AC-004/AC-007/AC-011/AC-013/AC-015. This class is genuinely closed.

4. FIELD DECLARATION ORDER PINNING (the PLAN-006 defect class) — verified INDEPENDENTLY and by mutation, not by inspection. All 6 types carry an "in this order" criterion. Each has a real order pin: exact-string assertions for the 5 structs (search_limits_/search_options_declaration_order_pinned_via_full_round_trip do parse-then-reserialize and assert byte-equality against a fixed literal; search_response_/symbols_result_/dependents_result_declaration_order_pinned_via_exact_serialize assert the full serialized string), and `as usize` discriminant casts for the fieldless Language enum. Critically, order is NOT left to be proven only by T-027's destructures or by BTreeSet-style key comparison — the exact-string assertions are separate and real.
   I proved they bite: I swapped adjacent fields in all six declarations. ALL 6 MUTANTS KILLED, each by its intended order test (Language variants, SearchLimits max_bytes<->max_tokens, SearchOptions limits<->exact, SearchResponse total_bytes<->total_tokens, SymbolsResult truncation_marker<->diagnostics, DependentsResult dependents<->imports). This class is genuinely closed too.

5. Six further semantic mutants, all killed: +Deserialize on SearchResponse (compile error); +Deserialize on SymbolsResult and on DependentsResult (each killed specifically by its *_serialize_only_no_deserialize test — this proves the pre-existing DeProbe absence-check genuinely bites rather than passing vacuously); +skip_serializing_if on SearchResponse.diagnostics; Default max_results Some(50)->Some(51); BTreeMap->HashMap on SymbolsResult.files; Option<Language>->Language.

6. serde_json error-string stress test — I wrote my OWN probe module and ran every boundary against real serde_json rather than trusting the plan. Every single spec claim reproduced exactly, including the counter-intuitive ones you flagged:
   - [1,2,3,4,1e309] -> "trailing characters", and explicitly NOT "number out of range". CONFIRMED. The out-of-range literal at position 4 is surplus input never reached by the per-element check.
   - ["a",1e309,3,4] -> "invalid type: string \"a\", expected usize" (position 0 wins over position 1's out-of-range literal). CONFIRMED.
   - [1,1e309,3,4] -> "number out of range". CONFIRMED.
   - [1,18446744073709551616,3,4] -> "invalid type: floating point `1.8446744073709552e+19`, expected usize". CONFIRMED.
   - 3-way numeric rendering: u64max -> "integer `18446744073709551615`"; u64max+1 -> "floating point `1.8446744073709552e+19`"; i64min-1 -> "floating point `-9.223372036854776e+18`"; 50.0 and 5e2 -> floating point; 1e309 -> "number out of range" with NO "expected struct SearchLimits" text. All CONFIRMED.
   - Length step: [] -> "invalid length 0, expected struct SearchLimits with 4 elements"; [1,2,3] -> "invalid length 3"; [50,100,null,5] and [null,2,null,4] both deserialize OK. CONFIRMED.
   - AC-005's load-bearing divergence: omitting maxResults/maxTokens yields None, NOT Some(50)/Some(20_000). Direction of the claim is CORRECT.
   - Default impl values exact: SearchLimits{Some(50), 2_097_152, Some(20_000), 1_000}; SearchOptions delegates to SearchLimits::default(), language: None.

7. Grep-anchor collision sweep — I ran all 46 of the plan's own grep -c/-cF anchors AND all 6 scoped `diff <(grep -B/-A ...)` structural checks against my FINAL fully-assembled file (the worst case for collisions). All pass; all 6 scoped diffs exit 0 with empty output. The author's decision to avoid bare repeated numeric literals (2_097_152, 20_000) as anchors is correct and was necessary.

8. Embedded cross-spec types correct: SearchResponse.results Vec<RankedBlock>, SymbolsResult.files BTreeMap<Utf8PathBuf, Vec<SymbolEntry>>, all three diagnostics Vec<Diagnostic>. All compile and serialize correctly against SPEC-003/005/006's already-committed types.

9. Seven dimensions: missing coverage NONE (all 16 ACs in some covers_criteria); wrong order NONE (strictly linear T-001..T-027, compiles at all 27 intermediate states); orphaned criteria NONE; missing error handling NONE (all 4 is_error_case criteria AC-003/AC-006/AC-010/AC-014 have tests); too large NONE (every task is grep + heredoc append + grep/diff verify + cargo test; largest is T-027 at ~9.2KB but still one paste — all well under 15 min); zero TBDs.

10. Append-only discipline honored — the real crates/monokl/src/types.rs and tests_types.rs remain UNTOUCHED at 482/1864 lines and git-clean after my entire review. All work was in my scratchpad.

== ISSUES (all non-blocking) ==

[1] task_id: T-027 | type: over-specified | description: Internal contradiction between consecutive steps. Step 4 ends with "Clean up: `rm -rf /tmp/spec007_fx`" while step 5 opens with "reuse the /tmp/spec007_fx fixture from the previous step (do not delete yet)". An implementer following step 4 literally destroys the fixture step 5 requires. | suggested_fix: Delete the trailing "Clean up: `rm -rf /tmp/spec007_fx`." sentence from T-027 step 4; step 5 already carries the final cleanup.

[2] task_id: ALL (T-001..T-027) | type: under-specified | description: Every task's fixture step sets `out=$( ... )` in one backticked command and then asserts in a SEPARATE backticked command: `echo "$out" | grep -q 'N passed; 0 failed' && echo PASSED_OK`. Shell state does not persist across separate invocations, so if each backticked command is run as its own call, $out is empty and the assert silently prints nothing instead of PASSED_OK. I reproduced this — it produces no output rather than a visible failure, making the check false-negative-prone. The preceding `tail -20` still shows the true result, so it degrades gracefully. | suggested_fix: Fold the assert into the same command block as the `out=$(...)` assignment, or tee to a file (`... > /tmp/spec007_fx/last.log`) and assert with `grep -q 'N passed; 0 failed' /tmp/spec007_fx/last.log && echo PASSED_OK`.

[3] task_id: T-011 | type: missing-error-handling | description: T-011 appends helper `fn valid_search_options_json() -> &'static str`, which has no caller until T-012. I reproduced the exact T-011 state and confirmed it emits `warning: function 'valid_search_options_json' is never used`. This is the ONLY one of the 27 intermediate states that is not warning-clean, so the plan's blanket 0-warning claim holds for the final state and 26 of 27 intermediates. Harmless at HEAD, but a per-task commit under `-D warnings` CI would fail at T-011. This is the only issue with any real teeth. | suggested_fix: Move `valid_search_options_json` from T-011's append block into T-012's, where its first caller lives; or note in T-011 that one dead_code warning is expected and resolved by T-012.

[4] task_id: ALL (fixture Cargo.toml) | type: under-specified (informational) | description: The /tmp fixture declares only `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"` and does not mirror the real workspace's `[workspace.lints.clippy] pedantic = warn` plus unwrap_used/expect_used/panic denials. I rebuilt the fixture with the real lint set: SPEC-007's additions produce 18 new clippy pedantic warnings (12 doc_markdown, 3 assertions_on_constants, 2 similar_names, 1 too_many_lines). None are errors (pedantic is warn-level), and the already-gated SPEC-003/005/006 baseline produces 98 warnings of the same classes — so this is consistent with accepted repo precedent and is NOT a regression. Flagged only because the plan's "0 warnings" claim is scoped to the fixture's weaker lint set, not the real crate's. | suggested_fix: Either add the workspace clippy block to the fixture Cargo.toml and restate the expectation as "no new clippy classes beyond the existing baseline", or scope the claim in the architecture field to "0 rustc warnings under the fixture lint set".

== BOTTOM LINE ==

Both defect classes that cost PLAN-005 and PLAN-006 extra cycles are closed here, and I confirmed each by independent inventory plus mutation testing rather than by reading the author's assurances. ## WHAT I ACTUALLY EXECUTED

Built my own isolated /tmp fixture crate (edition 2024; serde 1 + derive, serde_json 1 + preserve_order, camino 1 + serde1 → resolved 1.2.5, clap 4 + derive/env) mirroring src/lib.rs + src/types.rs + src/tests_types.rs, seeded from the real crates/monokl/src/{types.rs,tests_types.rs}. Verified SPEC-008's actual criteria myself rather than trusting the summary: confirmed TsconfigMode/WorkspaceOptions need no clap/serde involvement while ExtractRequest does derive Serialize+Deserialize.

Ran all 19 tasks in sequence, each with its own grep/diff verification commands run verbatim:
- Baseline 116 → final 132, exactly as claimed.
- EVERY intermediate count matched: 116,116,117,118,119,119,120,121,121,123,124,124,126,127,128,129,130,131,132.
- 0 build errors, 0 build warnings.
- clippy exit 0 (run with the real workspace lint config: pedantic=warn, unwrap/expect/panic=deny, plus lib.rs's `#![cfg_attr(test, allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic))]`).
- spec_hash 89ead59e...5f3bc1 matches current SPEC-008.json (sha256) exactly.

Three defect-class audits, by mutating types.rs and re-running the full suite (25 mutants total):
- CLASS 1 (field type pinning): 5/5 caught as compile errors — ExtractRequest.file Utf8PathBuf→String, line_start and line_end Option<usize>→Option<u64>, WorkspaceOptions.root Utf8PathBuf→String, TsconfigMode::Manual(Utf8PathBuf)→Manual(String). CLOSED.
- CLASS 2 (declaration order): 5/5 caught — TsconfigMode in two permutations, WorkspaceOptions field swap, ExtractRequest line_start/line_end swap, ExtractRequest file moved last. CLOSED.
- CLASS 3 (field-level serde attribute absence): 5/5 caught — #[serde(default)], #[serde(skip_serializing_if)], #[serde(rename)], #[serde(alias)] on individual fields, plus loss of type-level #[serde(rename_all)]. CLOSED.

Novel technique 1 — DefaultProbe (T-004): compiled it, then added `impl Default for TsconfigMode` to a throwaway copy. Probe flips and the test fails with `assertion failed: !DefaultProbe::<TsconfigMode>::IS`. Non-vacuous, TsData is a real positive control. SOUND.

Novel technique 2 — assert_attr_immediately_precedes_fn (T-010): tested three directions. (A) with_tsconfig loses #[must_use] → CAUGHT. (B) new gains #[must_use] directly above the fn → CAUGHT. (C) new gains #[must_use] above its DOC COMMENT → SURVIVED. Also verified the plan's premise is correct: #[must_use] is warning-only (compiled a discard call, saw `warning: unused return value ... that must be used`, exit 0), so a structural check genuinely is the only route.

Also: verified AC-012 against real camino 1.2.5 source (~/.cargo/registry/.../camino-1.2.5/src/serde_impls.rs) — Utf8PathBufVisitor::expecting writes exactly "a UTF-8 path string", method set is exactly visit_str/visit_string/visit_bytes/visit_byte_buf with no null override, so {"file": null} falls through to serde_json's default invalid-type error using that same text. Exactly as claimed. All 6 wrong-type strings pass verbatim, as do T-014/T-017's exact error strings including `1.8446744073709552e+19`, `-9.223372036854776e+18` and the 5e0→`5.0` normalization.

Spot-checked the plan's own verification commands against the FULLY ASSEMBLED final file (not just at each task's own point): T-001 -B1 -A4, T-005 -B1 -A3, T-011 -B2 -A4 all exit 0, and T-008's -A18 window still terminates exactly on the impl's closing brace after ExtractRequest was appended below it. No residual window-sizing bug. Collision sweep independently reproduced: all 4 types.rs anchors, all 4 enum_declaration_block needles, all 16 test-function names, both new helper names — count 1 each; no duplicate fn names anywhere.

## ISSUES

[1] task_id T-010 | type: missing-coverage | BLOCKING
description: assert_attr_immediately_precedes_fn has a real escape, and it is the same shape as defect class #3 (structural attribute check with too narrow a window) — the class that cost PLAN-007 three rounds. It tests only `block[..fn_pos].trim_end().ends_with(attr)`, i.e. the single token immediately before the fn signature. Mutant C (#[must_use] above new's doc comment) SURVIVES all 132 tests. This is a genuine AC-004 violation, not a technicality: I compiled it and confirmed rustc emits the unused_must_use warning for `WorkspaceOptions::new("x");`, so the attribute applies exactly as it does after the doc comment (attributes and doc comments are order-independent on an item).
suggested_fix: Widen from the immediately-preceding token to the item's whole attribute run, scanning attribute lines ONLY. Replace
    let preceding = block[..fn_pos].trim_end();
    let has_attr = preceding.ends_with(attr);
with
    let run_start = block[..fn_pos].rfind('}').map_or(0, |i| i + 1);
    let has_attr = block[run_start..fn_pos]
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|l| l.starts_with("#["))
        .any(|l| l.contains(attr));
Verified: clean source still passes, mutants A, B and C all now fail. Rename to assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run (or similar) — "immediately_precedes" is no longer what it checks — and update the doc comment.

[2] task_id T-019 | type: missing-coverage | BLOCKING
description: The Copy/PartialEq/Eq non-goal rests on a premise this plan's own T-004 refutes, and T-019's doc comment states that premise as fact in committed source. The cited precedent IS real — I read tests_types.rs:854-861, and spec_005_derive_lists_pinned does say "A generic bound check can only prove a trait IS implemented, not that it is absent," including the DependencyBinding example. But that is a limitation of BOUND-CHECK FUNCTIONS, not of the const-specialization probe. T-004 generalizes the probe to Default precisely to overcome that limitation, and the identical 4-line generalization works for Copy/PartialEq/Eq. I built CopyProbe/PartialEqProbe/EqProbe verbatim from DefaultProbe's shape: they pass on clean source and are non-vacuous — adding PartialEq to either type flips them and fails, with SymbolKind as a working positive control. Consequently the mutation "TsconfigMode gains PartialEq, Eq" SURVIVES all 132 tests, though AC-001 explicitly claims "no Copy, no PartialEq, no Eq" and AC-003 claims "#[derive(Debug, Clone)] only". T-019's sentence "it cannot prove the absence of Copy/PartialEq/Eq/non_exhaustive" is FALSE for Copy/PartialEq/Eq as of three tests earlier in the same file — shipping it writes a knowingly-incorrect justification into source. The plan's reasoning field compounds this: "CopyProbe/PartialEqProbe/NonExhaustiveProbe techniques do not exist anywhere in this codebase and building them here would be scope creep" — but T-004 creates exactly that technique, in this plan, and the extension is 12 lines. On the question you asked: the choice is documented openly in architecture, reasoning and T-019's doc comment — NOT swept under the rug. The problem is the stated reason, not concealment.
suggested_fix: Add CopyProbe/PartialEqProbe/EqProbe beside DefaultProbe in T-004 (each a 4-line copy), then in T-019 assert !CopyProbe::<TsconfigMode>::IS, !PartialEqProbe::<TsconfigMode>::IS, !EqProbe::<TsconfigMode>::IS, !CopyProbe::<WorkspaceOptions>::IS, !PartialEqProbe::<WorkspaceOptions>::IS, with SymbolKind as positive control for all three. Rewrite T-019's derive-list paragraph and the plan's reasoning/architecture fields to scope the acknowledged limitation to #[non_exhaustive] only. If the gap is kept deliberately, the doc comment must AT MINIMUM be corrected to say the technique exists and was declined — not that it is impossible.

[3] task_id T-019 | type: missing-coverage | BLOCKING
description: AC-001's #[non_exhaustive] absence claim has zero coverage. "TsconfigMode gains #[non_exhaustive]" SURVIVES all 132 tests (same for ExtractRequest, though AC-007 doesn't claim that one). T-001's scoped diff would catch it but is a plan-time command, not a committed regression test. This one genuinely cannot be closed with a probe — #[non_exhaustive] has no effect on matching within the defining crate, so it needs a structural source check.
suggested_fix: Once T-010's helper is widened per [1], reuse it directly against types.rs source:
    let src = include_str!("types.rs");

    },

      "id": "B-2",
      "criterion": "AC-002, AC-003",
      "severity": "high",
      "description": "The new structural checks match only the literal bare-`pub` spelling, so restricted-visibility variants evade them while violating the criteria as written. AC-003 claims 'a caller outside query/lexer.rs cannot call any of them directly' and AC-002 claims 'no code outside query/lexer.rs's own impl block can read... a Lexer's fields' -- pub(crate) makes both false.",
      "fix": "Replace the substring needles with a line-scoped prefix check. For methods: locate the line containing `fn {name}` inside the impl block and assert line.trim_start().starts_with(\"fn \") -- this rejects pub, pub(crate), and pub(super) uniformly. For fields: within the already-scoped field_block, assert each field's line trim_starts with `{field}:` rather than testing for the absence of one specific `pub ` spelling."
    },
    {
      "id": "B-3",
      "criterion": "AC-008",
      "severity": "medium",
      "description": "AC-008 requires Modifier to have 'exactly 3 variants in this order: Required, Excluded, Optional'. Adding a 4th variant `Extra` compiles and all 53 tests pass -- nothing pins the count. Token's equivalent AC-001 count claim is pinned for free, because parse()'s exhaustive match makes a 7th variant a compile error; Modifier is only compared with == in plan.rs, so no such protection exists. Variant order is also unpinned, and unlike Token -- whose data-carrying variants make order unobservable -- Modifier is fieldless, so its order IS observable and therefore testable.",
      "fix": "Add a Modifier test with an exhaustive match over a value (arms for Required/Excluded/Optional, no wildcard), making a 4th variant a compile error. Pin order in the same test via assert_eq!(Modifier::Required as isize, 0), Excluded as isize == 1, Optional as isize == 2."
    }
  ]
}

=== What I checked ===

1. Implementation unchanged. git diff 8fd7f2a..4573be3 on all four files touches only lines inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Every non-test line is byte-identical. The fix was genuinely test-only, as claimed.

2. Fresh fixture, real cargo test. Built my own isolated edition-2024 crate (lib.rs + error.rs + query/*.rs in the same relative layout so the include_str! calls resolve) at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl/a82f4f80-7822-4785-a872-33c66baeee45/scratchpad/fx. Result: 66 passed, 0 failed -- 53 in query::, 13 in error::. Note: the fix report's "67 tests" counts error.rs's miette-gated test; the query-module count is 53, of which 7 are new. Not a discrepancy that matters, just recording what I measured.

3. All 6 prior survivors are now dead. Each killed one at a time in a throwaway copy, by exactly the test written for it: (a) LIMIT-in-loop -> limit_check_runs_after_full_loop_...; (b) Token gains Eq/Hash/PartialOrd/Ord -> token_absence_of_...; (c) Lexer gains a derive -> lexer_struct_has_no_derive_...; (d) `pub fn read_word` -> lexer_helper_methods_are_private_...; (e) ParsedTerm gains PartialEq/Eq -> parsed_term_absence_of_...; (f) mod.rs leaks Lexer/Token -> mod_rs_exact_reexport_surface_structural. A bonus mutant (QueryPlan gains serde) is killed too.

4. Self-reference gotcha genuinely avoided. I read the check logic rather than trusting the note. lexer_struct_has_no_derive_... scopes the derive search to a window bounded by rfind("\n\n") before the declaration, and the field search to a brace-matched field_block -- not a whole-file scan -- and assembles field needles via format! so no literal appears in the test's own source. mod_rs_exact_reexport_surface_structural filters on trim_start().starts_with("pub use "), which correctly skips its own `let use_parser_pos = src.find(...)` lines, its vec![...] expected-value literal, and its // comment mentioning `pub use lexer::{Lexer, Token};`. I confirmed empirically that a multi-line `pub use lexer::{\n Lexer,\n Token,\n};` is still caught. No false positive found.

5. AC-022 genuinely discriminates. Injecting panic!("wrong reason") on the same reachable path makes the test FAIL -- the expected = "index out of bounds" string is doing real work, not passing on any panic.

6. Fresh adversarial scan (this is where the 3 blockers came from). Ran 14 further semantic mutations; 11 were caught: trim->trim_ascii, regex arm applying regex::escape, > -> >= on LIMIT, reversed from_terms order, scored-before-required chaining, chaining excluded in, is_empty checking required/scored, double-backslash treated as an escape, content_to_term forcing Optional, advance using += 1, and read_word stopping at '+'. Behavioral coverage is otherwise strong. The survivors became B-1 and B-3; the visibility probes became B-2.

7. All 22 criteria re-verified end to end against compiled output.

8. Commit scope clean. b85c4fd..4573be3 is 20 commits inclusive of b85c4fd (git log for the exclusive range shows 19). It touches exactly four files, all under crates/monokl/src/query/. Nothing outside it, no prior-spec content affected, working tree clean under crates/.

=== Two non-blocking notes ===

- A `pub  use lexer::{Lexer, Token};` leak with a double space evades mod_rs_exact_reexport_surface_structural's starts_with("pub use ") filter. Not calling this a blocker: it's cosmetic, cargo fmt normalizes it, and no plausible refactor produces it. Normalizing internal whitespace before the filter would close it for free if the implementer is in there anyway.
- One mutant I tried (hoisting the regex: check above the '+'/'-'/'"' arms) survives but is a TRUE EQUIVALENT MUTANT, not a gap: those branches are disjoint, since the regex: check can only fire when peek() == 'r'. AC-004's dispatch-order claim is unobservable by construction and needs no test. Please don't send this back to the implementer as work.

All three blockers are small, additive, test-only fixes in files already open. Recommend one more targeted round -- retry_count would be 3, which is the escalation threshold, so if a round 4 becomes necessary that should go to a human rather than cycling again.
