This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   This is a continuation of an extremely long spec-driven-development (SDD) session for "monokl," a Rust crate providing AST-aware semantic code search for AI coding agents, part of the "orin-axi" suite (alongside Firkin, Lumen, Pulse, and shared crate michi). The excerpt covered in this summary spans: SPEC-003's final implementation tasks and gate; the full plan→review→implement→mutate→gate cycles for SPEC-005 (an unusually costly 6-round gate saga), SPEC-006 (2 rounds, benefiting from SPEC-005's lessons), SPEC-007 (3 rounds, closing a recurring "field-attribute-absence" defect class for good), SPEC-008 (2 rounds), and SPEC-009 (still in progress — a structurally different, algorithmic-logic spec, currently on its 4th exit-gate cycle after a 3-retry escalation). Explicit user directives in this window, in order:
   - Implicit continuation through SPEC-003's remaining tasks and gate cycle (no new user message needed, following the standing "keep going through the sequence" authorization from before this window).
   - "Everything seems finished" / "You're not always getting notified it seems" — user flagged the recurring pattern of subagent idle-notifications arriving without their actual result; I confirmed this and established the "SendMessage direct check-in nudge" workaround as standard practice going forward.
   - "You've lost track of your agents somehow and you're wasting my money and tokens without results. wtf" — a sharp rebuke after SPEC-005's costly 6-round gate saga. I responded honestly (no agents were literally lost; the cost was real and I hadn't paused to check in), and offered 3 options.
   - "Let's keep dispatching and continue the work as autonomous as possible." — user's explicit choice, authorizing continued autonomous operation without further per-round check-ins.
   - "Can we move any faster??" — I explained the structural bottleneck (sequential one-task-at-a-time lambda-implementer dispatches per its own no-batching rule) and offered to lower the gate's acceptance bar as the main available lever.
   - "No, we don't want to lower the quality bar" — an explicit, standing rejection of that lever. Full adversarial rigor must be preserved; only communication/process efficiency may be optimized.
   - (Implicit, via not objecting) Confirmed continuation through SPEC-006, SPEC-007, SPEC-008 each following the same full-rigor cycle, with me checking in only at natural per-spec milestones (final PASS/FAIL reports), not mid-cycle.
   - "Is it running???" and "Been a while, where are you?" and "Still waiting?" and "The agents are not showing up so hard to tell" — a cluster of status-check messages during long-running planner/challenger dispatches for SPEC-009; I responded each time with honest, direct status (checking in via SendMessage rather than assuming completion).
   - (Local command) `/effort` → set effort level to "high" as saved default.
   - (Local command) `/plugin` then `/reload-plugins` with the message "Just reloaded plugins, let's make sure we're using the latest version" — I confirmed the agent-type renaming and switched to new names for all subsequent dispatches.
   - "What's the current status?" — I gave a full recap of all specs' pass/fail state.
   - "What happened?" — a request for a recap after SPEC-009's 3rd exit-gate FAIL and my presenting the AskUserQuestion escalation.
   - (AskUserQuestion answer) "Fix all 3 blockers, one more gate round" — user's explicit choice at SPEC-009's 3-retry escalation point, rejecting my recommended lighter option (fix B-1+B-2 only, waive B-3) in favor of full completeness on all 3 findings (including the low-severity, arguably-waivable declaration-order pinning for Token/ParsedTerm/QueryPlan).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **The full canon+axiom+vector+lambda pipeline**, unchanged from before: canon (spec drafting/gating) → axiom (independent cross-check) → vector (plan drafting via vector:planner, adversarial review via vector:challenger) → lambda (TDD implementation via lambda:recon → lambda:implementer [one task at a time, strict no-batching] → lambda:mutator → lambda:exit-gate [adversarial final verdict]).
   - **Post-plugin-reload agent naming**: agent type identifiers changed from doubled-prefix form (`vector:vector-challenger`, `lambda:lambda-implementer`, `canon:canon-drafter`, `axiom:axiom-exit-gate`) to de-duplicated short form (`vector:challenger`, `lambda:implementer`, `canon:drafter`, `axiom:exit-gate`). Old TaskCreate/TaskGet/TaskList/TaskUpdate MCP-backed tools became permanently disconnected around this same period ("The following deferred tools are no longer available (their MCP server disconnected)") — no more task-tracker updates possible from that point.
   - **The 3-retry escalation protocol**: lambda:exit-gate (and canon:exit-gate before it) has a standing rule: "Maximum 3 retries before escalation to a human reviewer" / escalates "when retry_count exceeds 3." Observed at SPEC-005 (implicitly, via extensive rounds), and explicitly triggered and handled via AskUserQuestion at SPEC-009's retry 3.
   - **The recurring "fix the named instance, not the whole class" failure pattern**: repeatedly observed across SPEC-005 (field-type pinning discovered piecemeal across 6 rounds), SPEC-007 (field-attribute-absence discovered for `skip_serializing_if` then re-discovered for `#[serde(default)]` before being closed via a general structural technique), and SPEC-009 (round 1 closed 6 named absence gaps; round 2 found 3 MORE in adjacent but untried mutation classes — case-sensitivity, pub(crate)/pub(super) variants, Modifier's variant count; round 3 found 3 MORE still — serde-absence on Token/Modifier/ParsedTerm, field-visibility on ParsedTerm/QueryPlan, declaration-order on all three). This pattern is now explicit institutional knowledge fed into every subsequent spec's planning brief.
   - **Established, reusable absence-proving and structural-pinning techniques** (all reused/generalized across SPEC-003/005/006/007/008/009):
     - `SerProbe`/`DeProbe`: const-specialization technique proving a type does NOT implement Serialize/Deserialize (a positive bound-check function can only prove presence, never absence — this exact limitation is documented in-repo, e.g. tests_types.rs ~line 1842-1850, ~3160).
     - `DefaultProbe`/`CopyProbe`/`PartialEqProbe`/`EqProbe`/`HashProbe`/`OrdProbe`/`PartialOrdProbe`: same const-specialization pattern generalized to other traits.
     - `enum_declaration_block`/`assert_declaration_order`: `include_str!("types.rs")`-style helpers that extract a named type's source block and assert field/variant names appear at strictly increasing text position, pinning declaration order — critical for types with data-carrying enum variants (where `as usize` discriminant casts don't apply) or types with no Serialize derive at all (where wire order can't reveal declaration order).
     - `assert_attr_in_item_attribute_run` (originally `assert_attr_immediately_precedes_fn`, renamed+widened after a real bug was found in PLAN-008's first review — it originally only checked the single line immediately preceding an item, missing attributes placed above a doc comment): scans an item's WHOLE attribute run (all `#[...]` lines back to the nearest preceding `}`) rather than just one line, used to pin method-level attributes like `#[must_use]` and type-level attributes like `#[non_exhaustive]`.
     - `assert_no_field_level_serde_attribute` (added during SPEC-007's 3rd fix round): structural check that no `#[serde(` line appears between consecutive field declarations — closes the whole "no field-level attribute" claim class in one shot rather than testing specific attribute types one at a time.
     - Line-scoped `trim_start().starts_with("fn ")` / `starts_with("pub {field}:")` privacy/visibility checks (introduced/refined across SPEC-009's fix rounds 1-3): the correct way to distinguish bare `pub`, `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, and fully-private, since naive substring search for `"pub "` misses `pub(crate)`/`pub(super)` variants, and checking only for presence of `pub` misses distinguishing `pub` from `pub(crate)` in the positive-visibility-required direction too.
   - **Empirical-plan-verification discipline**: every vector:planner dispatch since SPEC-005's lessons is instructed to build the ENTIRE plan's cumulative state in a real isolated fixture crate BEFORE finalizing, running cargo test at every task boundary, and re-deriving every grep/diff verification command from content proven to actually compile/pass — this consistently caught real bugs (grep-anchor collisions, scoped-diff window mis-sizing, a genuine parser behavioral surprise in SPEC-009's own draft).
   - **Isolated-fixture-crate testing pattern** (required throughout, since the real `crates/monokl` workspace cannot build): a standalone `/tmp` crate with its own bare `[workspace]` table (to escape ancestor Cargo workspaces), matching edition 2024, containing only the minimal files/dependencies needed for the spec under test (varies by spec: types.rs/tests_types.rs-based specs mirror `lib.rs`+`types.rs`+`tests_types.rs`; SPEC-009's query module mirrors `lib.rs`+`error.rs`+`query/*.rs`, explicitly NOT `types.rs`/`tests_types.rs` since it has no such dependency).
   - **cargo-mutants tool limitations discovered and empirically confirmed across this session** (documented for future specs' awareness): (1) `impl Default for T` blocks are unconditionally skipped (confirmed via reading cargo-mutants 27.1.0's own source, `src/visit.rs`); (2) an EARLIER claim that generic `impl Trait` parameters are generally skipped was found to be FALSE by a later, more rigorous gate pass — the real behavior is a NAME-based skip specifically on functions literally named `fn new`, confirmed via a controlled probe crate; (3) mutations that turn a state-advancing operation (e.g. `pos += 1`) into a no-op can cause an infinite loop, which cargo-mutants correctly classifies as `Timeout` (a legitimate "caught" outcome, not a coverage gap) — SPEC-009's mutation run had 18 such Timeout-classified mutants.
   - **SPEC-009's specific technical content** (query language, real algorithmic logic, NOT derive-heavy data types):
     - `crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs`: `Token` enum (6 variants: Plus, Minus, RegexPrefix, QuotedString(String), Word(String), Eof — `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]` only, explicitly no Eq/Hash/PartialOrd/Ord), `Lexer<'a>` struct (2 private fields `input`/`pos`, ZERO derive attributes of any kind — this is AC-002's headline claim), with exactly 2 public methods (`new`, `next_token`) and 6 private helper methods (`advance`, `peek`, `remaining`, `skip_whitespace`, `read_word`, `read_quoted`).
     - Lexer dispatch order in `next_token()`: `skip_whitespace()` always runs first; then `+`/`-`/`"` are checked (each consumes exactly 1 byte via `pos += 1`, using a peek-confirmed-ASCII shortcut); then the 6-byte literal `"regex:"` is checked (case-sensitive — this was the specific gap found in exit-gate round 2); then falls back to `read_word()`.
     - `read_word()`: greedy-until-whitespace consumption — `+`/`-`/`"` are only special AT token-start, never mid-word (so `"foo+bar"` tokenizes as one Word, not split).
     - `read_quoted()`: single-escape rule (only `\"` is a recognized escape; `\\` produces two literal backslashes, not an escape), silently tolerates an unterminated quoted string (no error, returns accumulated chars).
     - `crates/monokl/src/query/parser.rs`: `Modifier` enum (3 variants: Required, Excluded, Optional — fieldless, order IS observable/testable unlike Token), `ParsedTerm` struct (3 fields: `pattern`, `modifier`, `is_regex` — all `pub`, `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` only, no PartialEq/Eq, no serde), `parse(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<ParsedTerm>>` function, `content_to_term()` helper.
     - `parse()`'s exact behavior: empty/whitespace-only (including NBSP, since `str::trim()` treats it as Unicode whitespace, though `Lexer::skip_whitespace()` is ASCII-only — a deliberate, documented asymmetry) input returns `Ok(Vec::new())` via early return; the "swallowed lookahead token" pattern (`"+ +foo"` → one `Optional` term, `"regex: -foo"` → one `Optional` non-regex term "foo", both because the second modifier-prefix token is consumed as the FIRST prefix's lookahead content, hits `content_to_term`'s wildcard `_ => None` arm, and is silently dropped rather than reprocessed); a bare `regex:` prefix that never resolves to a word/quoted-string content produces ZERO terms; `"+regex:foo"`/`"-regex:foo"` degrade to an `Optional`, non-regex, escaped-literal term (content_to_term's `Token::RegexPrefix => None` arm fires, same swallow pattern); the LIMIT=64-terms cap check runs ONLY AFTER the main token-consuming loop fully completes (not incrementally inside it — this exact timing distinction was the SPEC-009 exit-gate round-1 finding, since an in-loop check with an early-return can never see the TRUE total count above the cap), producing `MonoklError::TooManyTerms { count: terms.len(), limit: 64 }` (using the crate's TRUE term count, not a capped value); regex pattern validity is NEVER checked at this layer (an invalid regex like `"regex:(unclosed"` parses successfully, unvalidated).
     - `crates/monokl/src/query/plan.rs`: `QueryPlan` struct (4 `pub` fields: `terms`, `required`, `excluded`, `scored` — `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` only, no serde), `from_terms(Vec<ParsedTerm>) -> Self` (partitions preserving relative order), `is_empty(&self) -> bool` (checks TOTAL `terms` count, not just required/scored — so an exclusion-only query is NOT `is_empty()`, even though `search_patterns()` on it returns an empty Vec — this divergence is AC-018's specific claim, tied to a documented finding #21), `search_patterns(&self) -> Vec<&str>` (required-then-scored category ordering, excluded omitted, each category's internal relative order preserved; panics on an out-of-bounds index if a QueryPlan is directly struct-literal-constructed with an invalid index — the type has no invariant-enforcement, by design, per AC-022).
     - `crates/monokl/src/query/mod.rs`: exactly 3 `pub mod` lines (lexer, parser, plan) then exactly 2 `pub use` lines (`pub use parser::{Modifier, ParsedTerm, parse};` and `pub use plan::QueryPlan;`) — `Lexer`/`Token` are deliberately NOT re-exported at the `query::` root level, only reachable via `query::lexer::`.

   - **SPEC-009's specific technical content** (query language, real algorithmic logic, NOT derive-heavy data types):

The single MISSED mutant is `src/query/parser.rs:91: delete match arm Token::RegexPrefix in content_to_term`. That is an **equivalent mutant** — `Token::RegexPrefix => None` and the following `_ => None` are semantically identical, so deleting the explicit arm cannot change behavior. Not a blocker. Important caveat: cargo-mutants' mutation catalog **structurally cannot express** derive-set changes, field visibility, declaration order, added methods, or dropped call arguments. ### BLOCKER 1 (high) — AC-019's directly-constructed-plan carve-out has zero coverage

AC-019 explicitly states: *"a QueryPlan can also be constructed directly by struct literal ... and in that case an excluded-looking term's pattern can appear in `search_patterns()`'s output if its index is placed in required or scored directly."* No test asserts this.

Surviving mutation at `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/query/plan.rs:28`:
```rust
self.required.iter().chain(self.scored.iter())
    .filter(|i| !self.excluded.contains(i))   // ADDED — behavior change
    .map(|&i| self.terms[i].pattern.as_str())
```
→ 65 passed, 0 failed. Every existing `search_patterns` test uses a `from_terms`-built plan where `excluded` never overlaps `required`/`scored`, so the added filter is invisible.

**Fix:** add a test constructing `QueryPlan { terms: vec![term(Modifier::Excluded, "e0"), term(Modifier::Required, "r0")], required: vec![0, 1], excluded: vec![0], scored: vec![] }` and assert `search_patterns() == vec!["e0", "r0"]`.

### BLOCKER 2 (high) — AC-010: `content_to_term`'s `Token::Word` arm's `regex::escape` is unpinned

Surviving mutation at `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/query/parser.rs:81-84` — `pattern: regex::escape(&w)` → `pattern: w` → 65 passed, 0 failed.

Every test reaching this arm uses an escape-identity input: `parse("+foo")`, `parse("+ foo")`, `parse("-foo")`. I confirmed empirically that `regex::escape("foo") == "foo"`. The sibling `QuotedString` arm of the *same function* IS covered (`minus_quoted_produces_excluded_escaped_term` uses `"a.b"`), so this is a sibling gap inside one function.

**Fix:** change `plus_word_produces_required_escaped_term` to `parse("+foo.bar")` and assert `terms[0].pattern == "foo\\.bar"`.

### BLOCKER 3 (high) — AC-012: the main loop's `Token::QuotedString` arm's `regex::escape` is unpinned

Surviving mutation at `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/query/parser.rs:61-65` — `pattern: regex::escape(&s)` → `pattern: s` → 65 passed, 0 failed.

The only test reaching this arm is `bare_word_and_quoted_string_produce_optional_escaped_terms`, whose quoted input is `"a b"`. I verified empirically that **`regex::escape("a b") == "a b"`** — a space is not a regex metacharacter. So the assertion `assert_eq!(terms[1].pattern, regex::escape("a b"))` is self-cancelling: both sides are identity, and it holds whether or not the implementation escapes. The sibling `Word` arm in the same loop IS covered (`"foo.bar"`).

**Fix:** change the quoted input to contain a metacharacter, e.g. `parse("foo.bar \"a.b\"")`, and assert the literal `"a\\.b"` rather than `regex::escape("a.b")` — a literal expectation cannot drift with the implementation.

### BLOCKER 4 (medium) — AC-003's "public API surface is exactly 2 methods" is not pinned

Surviving mutation in `/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs` — adding `pub fn current_pos(&self) -> usize { self.pos }` to the impl block → 65 passed, 0 failed.

`lexer_helper_methods_are_private_structural` proves the 6 named helpers are private and that `new`/`next_token` are pub, but cannot detect a 7th public method. This is the same class of gap that `mod_rs_exact_reexport_surface_structural` (`query/mod.rs:51-57`) already guards against — that test collects *all* `pub use` lines and `assert_eq!`s the whole vec specifically to catch an *extra* line. The technique exists in this codebase; it just was not applied to `lexer.rs`.

**Fix:** mirror it — collect every line inside `impl<'a> Lexer<'a>` containing `pub fn` and `assert_eq!` against exactly `["pub fn new", "pub fn next_token"]`.

### BLOCKER 5 (low) — AC-016's "`#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` only" is not fully pinned

Surviving mutation: `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]` on `QueryPlan` → 65 passed, 0 failed. `QueryPlan` carries only a serde-absence probe; `Token` by contrast carries a full `Eq`/`Hash`/`PartialOrd`/`Ord` absence battery.

I verified the escape surface is narrow: `#[derive(PartialEq)]` on `QueryPlan` is a compile error (`E0369` — `Vec<ParsedTerm>` has no `==` since `ParsedTerm` deliberately lacks `PartialEq`), and `Hash`/`Copy` likewise fail to compile. **`Default` is the only realistic undetected addition.** Lowest severity — reasonable to waive if you want to close this out.

**Explicitly NOT filed:** I checked the same class on `Modifier` (adding `Copy` + `Hash` survives), but AC-008's text for `Modifier` says "compiles with `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]`" *without* the word "only" that it uses for `ParsedTerm`. Blockers 1–3 are **behavioral and genuinely new** — none were raised in rounds 1–3, and each is proven by a surviving mutation that changes real observable output. # verdict@1 — SPEC-009, retry_count 6

**verdict: FAIL** · **confidence: high** · **artifact_type: implementation**

**verdict_summary:** B-001 and B-002 are genuinely closed. One new blocker: no test ever places whitespace inside a quoted string, leaving AC-006's wildcard-arm clause unpinned — two independent read_quoted mutations survive all 82 tests.

Done. Full reasoning below. Everything was re-derived from disk; no prior-round context inherited.

---

## 1. Fresh fixture + baseline

New isolated crate at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl/a82f4f80-7822-4785-a872-33c66baeee45/scratchpad/fix6` — bare `[workspace]`, edition 2024, `lib.rs` trimmed to `error` + `query` only, crates.io substitutes (camino/grep-regex/ignore/regex/serde/serde_json/thiserror) for the unresolvable orin-cargo-registry dep. No stale fixture reused.

**82 tests pass, 0 failures.** Count confirmed fresh, matches your expectation.

## 2. B-001 (AC-008, Modifier derive list) — CLOSED

`modifier_absence_of_copy_hash_partialord_ord_pinned` (`crates/monokl/src/query/parser.rs:157-168`) fails against each additive derive *individually*, not merely the combined mutation:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| `+ Copy` | FAILED (81 pass / 1 fail) |
| `+ Hash` | FAILED (81/1) |
| `+ PartialOrd, Ord` | FAILED (81/1) |
| all four at once | FAILED (81/1) |

Positive controls on `usize` present, so the probes aren't vacuously false. Clean revert → 82 pass.

## 3. B-002 (AC-003, Lexer public surface) — CLOSED

`lexer_exactly_two_public_methods_structural` (`crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:320-366`) catches all four variants I could construct:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| 2nd `impl<'a> Lexer<'a>` block carrying `pub fn position` | FAILED |
| `pub(crate) fn position` added to existing block | FAILED |
| bare `pub fn position` added to existing block | FAILED |
| existing helper `read_word` → `pub(crate) fn` | FAILED (2 tests) |

The `match_indices` + brace-depth rewrite genuinely fixed both the first-match-only and the `pub(crate)`-filter gaps retry-5 identified. Clean revert → 82 pass.

## 4. Mutation testing (cargo-mutants 27.1.0, scoped to the 4 query files)

51 mutants, 19m wall: **1 missed, 28 caught, 4 unviable, 18 timeouts.**

- The single miss is `src/query/parser.rs:91:9: delete match arm Token::RegexPrefix in content_to_term` — the **known equivalent** documented in prior rounds (falls through to `_ => None`, byte-identical behavior). Not re-flagged as a finding.
- The 4 unviable are `Default::default()` substitutions on types with no `Default` impl (`next_token`, `parse`, `content_to_term`, `from_terms`) — not survivors.
- All 18 timeouts are infinite-loop mutants where `self.pos` stops advancing (`+=` → `*=`/`-=`, `peek`/`advance` returning a constant, `skip_whitespace` → `()`). A hang is a detection, not a survival.
- **No new survivors from the automated pass.**

The other two known equivalents you flagged (the `'"'` arm `regex:` guard, and `from_terms`'s index-vector `.sort()`) did not appear in this mutant set — they were manual-probe findings from earlier rounds, not cargo-mutants output. Nothing to cross-check against.

## 5. Fresh adversarial sweep — NEW BLOCKER

I deliberately took angles prior rounds hadn't: error-field structure, mod.rs re-export exactness re-read fresh, the `read_quoted` × `read_word` boundary interaction, and the Unicode-vs-ASCII whitespace-definition divergence.

**Held up cleanly (all caught):** extra `pub use lexer::{Lexer, Token};` in mod.rs; `Lexer::new(input.trim())` in `parse`; `is_empty()` → `required.is_empty() && scored.is_empty()`; `skip_whitespace` → `char::is_whitespace`; `read_word` → `char::is_whitespace` (hangs, i.e. detected); dropping the escaped-quote `self.pos += 1`.

### B-003 (AC-006; sibling impact AC-012) — no test places ASCII whitespace inside a quoted string

Every quoted-string input in the suite has a whitespace-free payload: `"foo"`, `"ab"`, `"abc"`, `"a.b"`, `"a\"b"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a\` (unterminated), `"日本語"`. AC-006's wildcard clause — *"Any character other than a closing quote or a backslash is appended to the result as-is"* — is therefore unpinned for the exact character class that gives the quoting syntax its reason to exist.

AC-012 leans on this too: it grounds the only observable Word/QuotedString difference in *"which characters the original input's word-boundary and quote-escaping rules (AC-005, AC-006) allowed into the token's own String payload"* — which, given AC-005 stops `read_word` at exactly ASCII whitespace, is precisely whitespace.

Two independent, plausible mutations survive all 82 tests:

- **M1** — insert `Some(ch) if ch.is_ascii_whitespace() => break,` before `read_quoted`'s wildcard arm (`crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:74`). Quoted strings silently truncate at the first space. → **82 passed, 0 failed.**
- **M6** — insert `Some(ch) if ch == ' ' => {},` before the same wildcard arm. Spaces are silently dropped from the payload. → **82 passed, 0 failed.**

cargo-mutants generates neither shape, which is why five prior rounds plus this round's automated pass all missed it; it only surfaced under manual probing.

**Targeted fix — test-only, no implementation change.** Add to `crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs`'s `mod tests`:

```rust
// AC-006: a quoted string's wildcard arm appends ASCII whitespace as-is --
// the one character class that distinguishes a QuotedString payload from a
// Word's (AC-005 stops read_word at exactly these characters).
#[test]
fn quoted_string_contains_ascii_whitespace_verbatim() {
    let mut l = Lexer::new("\"a b\tc\"");
    assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::QuotedString("a b\tc".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::Eof);
}
```

Optionally a parser-level companion asserting `parse("\"a b\"")` yields exactly one Optional, non-regex term. **Caution for whoever writes it:** a `regex::escape("a b")` assertion self-cancels there (space is not a metacharacter), so the load-bearing assertion must be the token payload itself — hardcode `"a b"`. Same self-cancellation trap the earlier rounds hit.

## 6. Waiver recommendation

**Fix, don't waive.** It is the same class as the retry-4 and retry-5 findings — a behavior-changing mutation the suite doesn't kill — and closing it costs one ~6-line test with no implementation change and no risk to the other 82. It is not a spec-interpretation stretch: AC-006 states the requirement in its own text, and whitespace containment is the functional purpose of the quoting syntax. Waiving would leave the single most load-bearing property of `read_quoted` unpinned.

I'll note the round count explicitly since it matters for your escalation decision: this is round 6, and the blocker is genuinely new rather than a re-open of B-001/B-002 — the fix round did what it was asked to do. But the pattern is worth naming: each round's adversarial sweep has found one more gap of the same family, which suggests the marginal return is not yet zero but the remaining gaps are getting narrower and cheaper. If the human wants to cap the sequence, B-003 is small enough to fix in the same breath as making that call. Final call on waiving stays with the human.

## 7. Minor observations (explicitly NOT blockers)

- AC-020 states `parse("+café") == Ok(vec![ParsedTerm{Required, "café", false}])` as a concrete example. The suite covers the lexer half only (`Lexer::new("+café")` → Plus, Word). Compositionally implied by already-covered paths; not worth a round.
- `lexer_exactly_two_public_methods_structural`'s `match_indices("impl<'a> Lexer<'a> {")` also matches the string literal in its own source at `crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:323`, brace-matching a spurious second region over test code. It currently contributes zero lines and all four B-002 mutations are still caught — a robustness nit, not a correctness failure. Worth a comment if the file is touched again; not a fix on its own.

**Bottom line:** the two carried-forward blockers are genuinely closed. SPEC-009 is one small test away from complete and should not move to SPEC-010 until B-003 is closed.
</teammate-message>

I deliberately took angles prior rounds hadn't: error-field structure, mod.rs re-export exactness re-read fresh, the `read_quoted` × `read_word` boundary interaction, and the Unicode-vs-ASCII whitespace-definition divergence.

**Held up cleanly (all caught):** extra `pub use lexer::{Lexer, Token};` in mod.rs; `Lexer::new(input.trim())` in `parse`; `is_empty()` → `required.is_empty() && scored.is_empty()`; `skip_whitespace` → `char::is_whitespace`; `read_word` → `char::is_whitespace` (hangs, i.e. detected); dropping the escaped-quote `self.pos += 1`.

### B-003 (AC-006; sibling impact AC-012) — no test places ASCII whitespace inside a quoted string

Every quoted-string input in the suite has a whitespace-free payload: `"foo"`, `"ab"`, `"abc"`, `"a.b"`, `"a\"b"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a\` (unterminated), `"日本語"`. AC-006's wildcard clause — *"Any character other than a closing quote or a backslash is appended to the result as-is"* — is therefore unpinned for the exact character class that gives the quoting syntax its reason to exist.

AC-012 leans on this too: it grounds the only observable Word/QuotedString difference in *"which characters the original input's word-boundary and quote-escaping rules (AC-005, AC-006) allowed into the token's own String payload"* — which, given AC-005 stops `read_word` at exactly ASCII whitespace, is precisely whitespace.

Two independent, plausible mutations survive all 82 tests:

- **M1** — insert `Some(ch) if ch.is_ascii_whitespace() => break,` before `read_quoted`'s wildcard arm (`crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:74`). Quoted strings silently truncate at the first space. → **82 passed, 0 failed.**
- **M6** — insert `Some(ch) if ch == ' ' => {},` before the same wildcard arm. Spaces are silently dropped from the payload. → **82 passed, 0 failed.**

cargo-mutants generates neither shape, which is why five prior rounds plus this round's automated pass all missed it; it only surfaced under manual probing.

**Targeted fix — test-only, no implementation change.** Add to `crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs`'s `mod tests`:

```rust
// AC-006: a quoted string's wildcard arm appends ASCII whitespace as-is --
// the one character class that distinguishes a QuotedString payload from a
// Word's (AC-005 stops read_word at exactly these characters).
#[test]
fn quoted_string_contains_ascii_whitespace_verbatim() {
    let mut l = Lexer::new("\"a b\tc\"");
    assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::QuotedString("a b\tc".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::Eof);
}
```

Optionally a parser-level companion asserting `parse("\"a b\"")` yields exactly one Optional, non-regex term. **Caution for whoever writes it:** a `regex::escape("a b")` assertion self-cancels there (space is not a metacharacter), so the load-bearing assertion must be the token payload itself — hardcode `"a b"`. Same self-cancellation trap the earlier rounds hit.

## 6. Waiver recommendation

**Fix, don't waive.** It is the same class as the retry-4 and retry-5 findings — a behavior-changing mutation the suite doesn't kill — and closing it costs one ~6-line test with no implementation change and no risk to the other 82. It is not a spec-interpretation stretch: AC-006 states the requirement in its own text, and whitespace containment is the functional purpose of the quoting syntax. Waiving would leave the single most load-bearing property of `read_quoted` unpinned.

I'll note the round count explicitly since it matters for your escalation decision: this is round 6, and the blocker is genuinely new rather than a re-open of B-001/B-002 — the fix round did what it was asked to do. But the pattern is worth naming: each round's adversarial sweep has found one more gap of the same family, which suggests the marginal return is not yet zero but the remaining gaps are getting narrower and cheaper. If the human wants to cap the sequence, B-003 is small enough to fix in the same breath as making that call. Final call on waiving stays with the human.

## 7. Minor observations (explicitly NOT blockers)

- AC-020 states `parse("+café") == Ok(vec![ParsedTerm{Required, "café", false}])` as a concrete example. The suite covers the lexer half only (`Lexer::new("+café")` → Plus, Word). Compositionally implied by already-covered paths; not worth a round.
- `lexer_exactly_two_public_methods_structural`'s `match_indices("impl<'a> Lexer<'a> {")` also matches the string literal in its own source at `crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:323`, brace-matching a spurious second region over test code. It currently contributes zero lines and all four B-002 mutations are still caught — a robustness nit, not a correctness failure. Worth a comment if the file is touched again; not a fix on its own.

**Bottom line:** the two carried-forward blockers are genuinely closed. SPEC-009 is one small test away from complete and should not move to SPEC-010 until B-003 is closed.

1	# monokl
2	
3	AST-aware semantic code search for TypeScript, JavaScript, and Rust — built for AI coding agents, not humans reading a terminal.
4	
5	> **Status: spec-stage.** No code exists yet. The full design lives in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md); this repo is where that spec gets implemented. If you're looking for something to run, there isn't one yet — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for where things stand.
6	
7	## What it does
8	
9	Grep finds text. Embeddings find _vibes_. monokl parses your code with a real compiler-grade parser ([OXC](https://oxc.rs) for TS/JS, [`ra_ap_syntax`](https://crates.io/crates/ra_ap_syntax) for Rust) and answers structural questions:
10	
11	```
12	mnkl search "validatePrice" --path src/
13	mnkl refs Button --root . --include-tests
14	mnkl definition useCart --root .
15	mnkl dependents src/utils/format.ts --root .
16	mnkl explain src/components/Button.tsx
17	```
18	
19	Text search ranks by BM25 and node-type relevance, not string distance. `refs`/`definition` resolve real bindings, not name matches. `dependents` walks an actual import graph. Everything returns structured JSON by default, with a JSON Schema per result type — built to be a tool an agent calls, not a report a human scrolls through.
20	
21	## Why
22	
23	Existing code-search-for-agents tools mostly fall into two camps: fast-but-fuzzy (grep, embeddings) or precise-but-heavyweight (a full language server, a persistent daemon). monokl aims at the middle — real AST parsing without the cost of running a language server, no persistent index to keep warm, cache-friendly enough that repeat queries in one session don't re-pay the parse cost. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how, and [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) for why it's built this way instead of the alternatives.
24	
25	## Language support
26	
27	| Language | Parser | Status |
28	| --- | --- | --- |
29	| TypeScript / JavaScript | OXC | Fully specified |
30	| Rust | `ra_ap_syntax` | Fully specified |
31	| Python | tree-sitter-python | Specified, not implemented |
32	| Go | [`gosyn`](https://github.com/chikaku/gosyn) | Specified, not implemented |
33	| Java | tree-sitter-java | Specified, not implemented |
34

1	# monokl
2	
3	AST-aware semantic code search for TypeScript, JavaScript, and Rust — built for AI coding agents, not humans reading a terminal.
4	
5	> **Status: spec-stage.** No code exists yet. The full design lives in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md); this repo is where that spec gets implemented. If you're looking for something to run, there isn't one yet — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for where things stand.
6	
7	## What it does
8	
9	Grep finds text. Embeddings find _vibes_. monokl parses your code with a real compiler-grade parser ([OXC](https://oxc.rs) for TS/JS, [`ra_ap_syntax`](https://crates.io/crates/ra_ap_syntax) for Rust) and answers structural questions:
10	
11	```
12	mnkl search "validatePrice" --path src/
13	mnkl refs Button --root . --include-tests
14	mnkl definition useCart --root .
15	mnkl dependents src/utils/format.ts --root .
16	mnkl explain src/components/Button.tsx
17	```
18	
19	Text search ranks by BM25 and node-type relevance, not string distance. `refs`/`definition` resolve real bindings, not name matches. `dependents` walks an actual import graph. Everything returns structured JSON by default, with a JSON Schema per result type — built to be a tool an agent calls, not a report a human scrolls through.
20	
21	## Why
22	
23	Existing code-search-for-agents tools mostly fall into two camps: fast-but-fuzzy (grep, embeddings) or precise-but-heavyweight (a full language server, a persistent daemon). monokl aims at the middle — real AST parsing without the cost of running a language server, no persistent index to keep warm, cache-friendly enough that repeat queries in one session don't re-pay the parse cost. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how, and [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) for why it's built this way instead of the alternatives.
24	
25	## Language support
26	
27	| Language | Parser | Status |
28	| --- | --- | --- |
29	| TypeScript / JavaScript | OXC | Fully specified |
30	| Rust | `ra_ap_syntax` | Fully specified |

2	
3	This is the design in prose. For verbatim code, see [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md).
4	
5	## Two levels: analyze once, aggregate separately
6	
7	Every file gets parsed exactly once, by a `LanguageAnalyzer`:
8	
9	```
10	file → LanguageAnalyzer::analyze() → FileAnalysis (owned: symbols, deps, exports, code blocks)
11	```
12	
13	`FileAnalysis` never borrows from the parser's arena — everything in it is owned data (`String`, not `&str`; `Vec<T>` of owned items). The arena drops at the end of `analyze()`. This is a hard rule, not a style preference: it's what lets `FileAnalysis` be cached, shared across threads via `Arc`, and outlive the parse call that produced it.
14	
15	A second layer, `WorkspaceEnricher`, folds per-file analyses into workspace-wide structure — an import graph, a symbol index — without re-parsing anything:
16	
17	```
18	Vec<FileAnalysis> → WorkspaceEnricher::update() × N files → WorkspaceIndex
19	```
20	
21	Two enrichers exist today: `ImportGraphEnricher` (which files import which) and `SymbolIndexEnricher` (symbol name → declaration sites). Both are cheap bookkeeping over already-parsed data — the expensive part is parsing, done once, upstream.
22	
23	Building a `WorkspaceIndex` is three phases:
24	
25	1. **Parallel analyze.** Walk the directory, run `LanguageAnalyzer::analyze()` per file via `rayon`, then sort by path — sorting _after_ parallel completion, not enforcing commit order _during_ it, because import resolution is real (`oxc_resolver`, not name-matching), so there's no candidate-disambiguation-by-insertion-order problem to solve in the first place.
26	2. **Stream `update()`** for every (file, enricher) pair.
27	3. **`finalize()`** each enricher — by now the full file index exists, so an enricher can resolve `Utf8PathBuf → FileIdx` for edges it deferred during `update()`.
28	
29	## The search pipeline
30	
31	`search` is eight stages, each one doing strictly less work on strictly fewer candidates than the last:
32	
33	1. Parse the query (`+required` / `-excluded` / bare-optional / `"phrase"` / `regex:pattern`).
34	2. Canonicalize the workspace root.
35	3. Text prefilter — `grep-searcher` (the crate ripgrep is built on) over the candidate file set.
36	4. Boolean evaluation — drop files missing a required term or containing an excluded one.
37	5. Block retrieval — analyze surviving files, keep only code blocks overlapping a matched line.
38	6. BM25 rank (`K1=1.5`, `B=0.5`) plus a node-type boost (functions rank higher than modules) and a coverage boost (more of the block matched = higher).
39	7. Dedup — drop blocks that overlap >50% with a higher-ranked block in the same file.
40	8. Token budget — truncate to fit, with an explicit marker so an agent knows results were cut.
41	
42	Every stage is designed to fail toward "fewer, better results" rather than "more results, sort it out downstream" — the token budget in stage 8 is a last resort, not the primary filter.
43	
44	## Caching: two tiers, one invariant
45	
46	```
47	stat(path) → mtime + size match? → return cached, no file read
48	           → no match → read file → blake3 hash → hash match? → refresh mtime, return cached
49	                                                  → no match → re-parse, cache result
50	```
51	
52	`ContentHash` (blake3) is authoritative; mtime/size is the cheap dirty-bit that avoids reading files that haven't actually changed. 4	
5	monokl is spec-stage — no `Cargo.toml`, no `src/`, nothing to build or run yet. The design is fully written up in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md). The other four spec files are the source of truth for _what_ to build; this one is the source of truth for _why_ it looks the way it does.
8	
9	## Proposing a spec change
10	
11	Don't silently edit around a design decision you disagree with. Add a dated entry to `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md` explaining what changed and why — same discipline that's already been applied throughout that file. If the change is substantial enough to need its own writeup, add a new file under `docs/spec/` and link it from [`docs/spec/README.md`](docs/spec/README.md).
12	
13	## Once there's code
14	
15	These conventions are already locked into the spec — `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md`'s workspace lint table — and apply from the first commit, not as an aspiration to grow into:
16	
17	- **No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!()`, `unreachable!()`, or `unimplemented!()` in library code.** Denied at the workspace level via `clippy`. Fine in `#[cfg(test)]` code — assertions are supposed to panic on failure there.
18	- **`thiserror`, one error enum per crate**, composed via `#[from]`/`#[source]` rather than proliferating string-message variants. See `MonoklError` in [`docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md`](docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md) for the pattern.

21	- **`cargo nextest`** for running tests, **`insta`** for snapshot tests.
22	
23	## Filing an issue
24	
25	Say what you expected, what happened, and — if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch — which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading. "The spec says X but Y happens" is more actionable than "this is broken."
26

1	# Principles
2	
3	What monokl believes, and why. See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) for how these get built.
4	
5	## Design tenets
6	
7	**Parse once, use everywhere.** A single `FileAnalysis` cache feeds every command — `search`, `symbols`, `refs`, `definition`, all of it. No command re-parses a file another command already analyzed in the same run.
8	
9	**Aggregate views, not re-scans.** The import graph and symbol index are folded from cached per-file data by `WorkspaceEnricher`s. Building workspace-wide structure never means re-walking the filesystem or re-reading files that are already cached.
10	
11	**Token budget is non-negotiable.** `max_bytes` has a hard 2MB ceiling. When output gets truncated, the response says so explicitly — a truncation marker, not silent data loss. An agent consuming monokl's output should never have to guess whether it's seeing everything.
12	
13	**Determinism.** Serialized output uses `BTreeMap` for stable key order. Ties break on `(file, line_start)`. BM25 scores round to 6 decimal places specifically to eliminate floating-point divergence between x86-64 and ARM64 — the same query against the same code should produce byte-identical JSON regardless of what machine ran it.
14	
15	**Arena lifetime containment.** No AST node born from the parser's `Allocator` escapes a per-file `analyze()` call. Every field on `FileAnalysis` is owned. This isn't a style preference — it's what makes caching and cross-thread sharing possible at all.
16	
17	**Graceful degradation.** A broken file sets `had_parse_errors = true` and still contributes whatever data survived — it doesn't abort the whole operation. An unsupported language emits a `Skipped` diagnostic — it doesn't crash or silently return nothing.
18	
19	**Tier separation.** Level 1 (`LanguageAnalyzer`, per-file) produces. Level 2 (`WorkspaceEnricher`, per-workspace) folds. Neither layer does the other's job.
20	
21	**Content hash is authoritative.** `blake3` over file content is the real cache key. `mtime`/ `size` is the cheap fast-path check that avoids reading files that haven't changed — never the source of truth on its own.
22	
23	## Non-goals
24	
25	Deliberately not built, and why:
26	
27	- **A persistent on-disk search index** (tantivy-style). The cache remembers parses; it doesn't maintain a standing inverted index. Simpler, and the numbers so far say it's fast enough without one below ~50k files — see [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md).
28	- **A full [Salsa](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa) incremental-computation framework.** Real precedent exists for using Salsa standalone (Astral's `ty`, Biome), decoupled from rust-analyzer's own query set — this is an open investigation track, not a closed door.
29	- **Embedding-based retrieval by default.** No code-specific evidence it beats lexical + structural signals for single-codebase search, and it would mean either bundling a model or calling a cloud API — both in tension with staying local-first and low-latency. Gate behind an explicit opt-in if it's ever added; don't make it the default posture.
30	- **Stemming.** Code identifiers aren't prose; stemming rules built for English text don't transfer.
31	- **An in-memory trigram index.** Tried, measured, rejected — 600MB–1.2GB resident at scale in an earlier design. The current `WorkspaceIndex` design lands at roughly 90–140MB at 50k files by comparison.
32	- **Tree-sitter for TypeScript/JavaScript.** OXC is the native, arena-owned, actively-maintained alternative already chosen — no reason to trade that for a generic multi-language parser framework on the one language that has a better option.
33	- **A running agent loop.** monokl is a tool an agent calls, not an agent itself.
34	
35	## Language coverage isn't uniform, and shouldn't pretend to be
36	
37	A language gets a native parser and full `Structural`/`Exact` precision when it earns that investment — not by default, and not on a fixed roadma...
[/external_agent_tool_result]

1	# Architecture
2	
3	This is the design in prose. For verbatim code, see [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md).
4	
5	## Two levels: analyze once, aggregate separately
6	
7	Every file gets parsed exactly once, by a `LanguageAnalyzer`:
8	
9	```
10	file → LanguageAnalyzer::analyze() → FileAnalysis (owned: symbols, deps, exports, code blocks)
11	```
12	
13	`FileAnalysis` never borrows from the parser's arena — everything in it is owned data (`String`, not `&str`; `Vec<T>` of owned items). The arena drops at the end of `analyze()`. This is a hard rule, not a style preference: it's what lets `FileAnalysis` be cached, shared across threads via `Arc`, and outlive the parse call that produced it.
14	
15	A second layer, `WorkspaceEnricher`, folds per-file analyses into workspace-wide structure — an import graph, a symbol index — without re-parsing anything:
16	
17	```
18	Vec<FileAnalysis> → WorkspaceEnricher::update() × N files → WorkspaceIndex
19	```
20	
21	Two enrichers exist today: `ImportGraphEnricher` (which files import which) and `SymbolIndexEnricher` (symbol name → declaration sites). Both are cheap bookkeeping over already-parsed data — the expensive part is parsing, done once, upstream.
22	
23	Building a `WorkspaceIndex` is three phases:
24	
25	1. **Parallel analyze.** Walk the directory, run `LanguageAnalyzer::analyze()` per file via `rayon`, then sort by path. Sorting happens _after_ parallel completion rather than enforcing commit order _during_ it — import resolution is real (`oxc_resolver`, not name-matching), so there's no insertion-order ambiguity to guard against.
26	2. **Stream `update()`** for every (file, enricher) pair.
27	3. **`finalize()`** each enricher — by now the full file index exists, so an enricher can resolve `Utf8PathBuf → FileIdx` for edges it deferred during `update()`.
28	
29	## The search pipeline
30	
31	`search` is eight stages, each one doing strictly less work on strictly fewer candidates than the last:
32	
33	1. Parse the query (`+required` / `-excluded` / bare-optional / `"phrase"` / `regex:pattern`).
34	2. Canonicalize the workspace root.
35	3. Text prefilter — `grep-searcher` (the crate ripgrep is built on) over the candidate file set.
36	4. Boolean evaluation — drop files missing a required term or containing an excluded one.
37	5. Block retrieval — analyze surviving files, keep only code blocks overlapping a matched line.
38	6. BM25 rank (`K1=1.5`, `B=0.5`) plus a node-type boost (functions rank higher than modules) and a coverage boost (more of the block matched = higher).
39	7. Dedup — drop blocks that overlap >50% with a higher-ranked block in the same file.
40	8. Token budget — truncate to fit, with an explicit marker so an agent knows results were cut.
41	
42	Every stage is designed to fail toward "fewer, better results" rather than "more results, sort it out downstream" — the token budget in stage 8 is a last resort, not the primary filter.
43	
44	## Caching: two tiers, one invariant
45	
46	```
47	stat(path) → mtime + size match? → return cached, no file read
48	           → no match → read file → blake3 hash → hash match? → refresh mtime, return cached
49	                                                  → no match → re-parse, cache result
50	```
51	
52	`ContentHash` (blake3) is authoritative; mtime/size is the cheap dirty-bit that avoids reading files that haven't actually changed. Two storage layers: an in-memory `DashMap` (process-local, lock-free reads) for repeat calls within one run, and a disk-persisted `.monokl/cache.json` (version- and config-hash-gated, so a monokl upgrade or a tsconfig change invalidates it automatically) for repeat calls across separate CLI invocations.
53	
54	There's deliberately no persistent on-disk _search_ index (no tantivy-style inverted index, no SQLite). The cache remembers _parses_; the `WorkspaceIndex` (import graph, symbol index) is rebuilt in memory on every invocation from the cached per-file data — cheap, because it's aggregation over alrea...

SPEC-009 exit-gate pass 8 is COMPLETE. Verdict: FAIL, retry_count 8. One genuine blocker (B-007) plus two optional hardening items. Repo working tree untouched — all mutation work was done in an isolated fixture.

=== verdict@1 ===
verdict: fail
confidence: high
artifact_type: implementation
retry_count: 8
verdict_summary: "Fresh fixture 86/86 pass; B-004/005/006 confirmed closed. Class sweep found B-007: the 'regex:' prefix literal's trailing colon is unpinned — starts_with(\"regex\") survives all 86 tests and silently makes parse(\"regexp\") return zero terms."

=== 1. Fresh fixture and baseline ===
Built a NEW fixture crate at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl/a82f4f80-7822-4785-a872-33c66baeee45/scratchpad/fx8 — own bare [workspace] table, edition 2024, lib.rs trimmed to error+query only, error.rs plus all four query/*.rs mirrored, crates.io substitutes for the orin-cargo-registry deps (thiserror 2, serde, serde_json, camino, ignore, regex, grep-regex). No stale fixture reused.

Result: 86 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Confirms the expected count fresh.

=== 2. B-004 / B-005 / B-006 independently re-verified as closed ===
Re-applied each documented violation separately against the fresh fixture; each was caught by exactly one test, with a clean revert to 86-pass verified after each (and lexer.rs confirmed byte-identical to the repo copy afterward):

- B-004 — read_word predicate narrowed to `ch == ' '` -> caught by `word_stops_at_every_ascii_whitespace_kind_not_just_space` (85 passed / 1 failed)
- B-005 — `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` placed on its own line with a blank-line separator above `pub struct Lexer<'a>` (the exact placement that evades the structural text-window check) -> caught by `lexer_implements_none_of_the_common_derivable_traits_pinned` (85/1)
- B-006 — a second `impl Lexer<'_> { pub fn sneaky_pos(&self) -> usize { .. } }` block using the elided-lifetime spelling -> caught by `lexer_exactly_two_public_methods_structural` (85/1)

All three fixes hold. The retry-7 round's findings are genuinely closed, not papered over.

=== 3. Class-level predicate-narrowing sweep (the main ask) ===
I manually enumerated every boolean predicate, comparison operator, arithmetic site, threshold constant, and literal comparison across lexer.rs / parser.rs / plan.rs — not just the ones already tested — and checked each against a plausible narrower/wider/off-by-one/substituted variant rather than only wholesale deletion or negation.

Confirmed genuinely pinned (spot-checked by reasoning, and by mutation where non-obvious):
- skip_whitespace's is_ascii_whitespace: narrowing to `ch == ' '` is killed by next_token_skips_leading_ascii_whitespace_unconditionally; WIDENING to Unicode `is_whitespace()` is killed by nbsp_prefixed_word_is_not_trimmed_away_and_lexer_keeps_the_nbsp. Both directions covered.
- read_word's is_ascii_whitespace: narrowing killed by the new B-004 test; widening to Unicode killed by the same NBSP test.
- read_quoted's `'"'` terminator, `'\\'` escape trigger, inner `peek() == '"'`, and the escaped-quote `pos += 1` (both +=0 and +=2 die) — all pinned by AC-006 examples 1-4.
- advance()'s `pos += ch.len_utf8()`: `+= 1` dies on the multi-byte tests (日本語 slices at a non-boundary).
- next_token's '+' / '-' / '"' dispatch chars and their 1-byte increments: pinned, the first two by explicit `assert_eq!(l.pos, 1)`.
- `pos += "regex:".len()`: 5 or 7 die on `assert_eq!(l.pos, 6)`.
- `remaining()` vs `self.input` in the prefix check: substituting self.input dies on plus_regex_prefix_degrades_to_optional_escaped_literal_foo (pos is 1 there, not 0).
- parse's `input.trim().is_empty()`: reducing to `input.is_empty()` dies on nbsp_only_input_returns_empty_vec_via_unicode_trim.
- LIMIT = 64 and the strict `>`: 63 dies on exactly_64_terms_succeeds, 65 dies on the 65-term test, `>=` dies on exactly_64; and count==100 pins that the check runs after the full loop.
- All four regex::escape sites: each assertion uses an input containing a real metacharacter ('.'), so even the ones written as a re-computed `regex::escape("a.b")` do NOT self-cancel. Verified individually.
- from_terms' three Modifier equality filters, search_patterns' chain order, and its `self.terms[i]` indexing: all pinned by the partition/order tests.
- plan.rs is_empty: the REALISTIC mis-implementation AC-018 explicitly warns about (`required.is_empty() && scored.is_empty()`) IS caught by the exclusion-only assertion.

The sweep surfaced three survivors. One is material.

=== B-007 (BLOCKER) — crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:88 ===
AC-004 requires the check be against "the exact, case-sensitive 6-byte literal 'regex:'". Prior rounds pinned the case-sensitive half (REGEX:, Regex: tests) and the 6-byte half (assert_eq!(l.pos, 6)) — but never the COLON. Every test input either supplies the full "regex:" or does not begin with "regex" at all, so nothing distinguishes the real literal from a colonless variant.

Mutating `self.remaining().starts_with("regex:")` -> `starts_with("regex")` SURVIVES all 86 tests.

Measured behavioral consequence (not reasoned — I ran both):
  TRUE:    lex("regexp") = Word("regexp");  parse("regexp") = [ParsedTerm{Optional, "regexp", is_regex:false}]
  MUTANT:  lex("regexp") = RegexPrefix;     parse("regexp") = []      <-- zero terms, silently
(The increment stays 6, so "regexp" is consumed entirely, RegexPrefix is emitted, then pattern_tok is Eof and the wildcard arm drops it.) "regexes", "regexbuilder", etc. degrade identically. A user searching for "regexp" gets a silently empty result set — a real, wrong, undiagnosed search result.

Fix (I verified it: passes clean on unmutated code and kills the mutant). Add to lexer.rs's test module:

    // AC-004: the "regex:" prefix check requires the trailing colon -- a word
    // merely STARTING with "regex" is an ordinary Word. Every other regex-prefix
    // test in this file either supplies the full 6-byte literal or an input that
    // doesn't begin with "regex" at all, so none can distinguish the real literal
    // from a colonless `starts_with("regex")` variant.
    #[test]
    fn regex_prefix_requires_the_trailing_colon() {
        let mut l = Lexer::new("regexp");
        assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::Word("regexp".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::Eof);
        let mut l2 = Lexer::new("regex foo");
        assert_eq!(l2.next_token(), Token::Word("regex".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(l2.next_token(), Token::Word("foo".to_string()));
    }

(Optionally mirror end-to-end in parser.rs with parse("regexp") -> one Optional non-regex term with pattern "regexp".)

=== Optional hardening (your call, same as B-005/B-006 last round) ===
- B-008 — lexer.rs:50. The B-004 test covers \t \n \r but NOT form feed (0x0C), which is_ascii_whitespace() includes. A hand-rolled `matches!(ch, ' '|'\t'|'\n'|'\r')` predicate survives all 86. Fix: `word_stops_at_form_feed` on "foo\x0Cbar". Lower realism than B-007 — excluding exactly form-feed while keeping \r is not a natural code shape.
- B-009 — plan.rs:25. `is_empty()` -> `self.terms.len() <= 1` survives (tests only exercise 0-term and 2-term plans). Fix: a single-term `assert!(!qp.is_empty())`. Low realism — an off-by-one inside an is_empty is an unnatural shape.
I verified both proposed tests pass clean and kill their mutants; with all three added the suite is 89/89.

One more I judged NOT worth raising: AC-002 says Lexer carries no derive "of any kind", and the 9 trait probes cover the common std derivables but not serde. A `#[derive(Serialize)]` would still be caught by the structural window check unless ALSO placed with a blank-line separator. Implausible derive x unnatural placement — not a real gap.

=== 4. Mutation testing (cargo-mutants 27.1.0, scoped to src/query/*.rs) ===
51 mutants: 28 caught, 4 unviable, 18 timeouts, 1 missed.
- The 1 MISSED is `src/query/parser.rs:91: delete match arm Token::RegexPrefix in content_to_term`. This is provably EQUIVALENT — deleting the arm falls through to the adjacent `_ => None`, returning the same value. Not a gap. (Consistent with prior rounds.)
- The 18 timeouts are all non-terminating mutants (pos decrements/multiplications, read_word returning "" without advancing) that hang the parse loop. A hanging implementation is detected by the suite; cargo-mutants just doesn't score it as "caught".

Crucially, this run CONFIRMS the structural blind spot the retry-7 gate identified. cargo-mutants generated no mutation of the "regex:" string literal's CONTENT at all — its repertoire is guard->true, delete-arm, arithmetic-operator swap, and return-value replacement. It cannot substitute string-literal contents, which is exactly why six prior clean runs plus this seventh gave false reassurance on B-007. The manual sweep was the only thing that could have found it.

=== 5. Fresh adversarial sweep across all 22 ACs ===
Re-derived each criterion from the spec and re-checked coverage from scratch. AC-001 through AC-022 are otherwise fully and correctly pinned — including the Token exhaustive-match variant-count guarantee (parser.rs's main loop has no wildcard, so a 7th variant is a compile error), Modifier's discriminant-order assertions, the AC-019 direct-construction carve-out, AC-022's OOB panic, and AC-021's mod.rs surface. AC-010/AC-011 have minor untested-but-equivalent input variants (Minus-as-content, Plus-as-pattern_tok) that route through the same already-tested wildcard arms — adequate, not gaps. The only defective criterion is AC-004, via B-007.

=== 6. Honest assessment of B-007's nature ===
B-007 is NOT a new defect class. It is a bounded, closeable instance of the SAME class as B-003/B-004: a predicate or literal where every existing test input satisfies both the true form and a plausible variant, so the variant survives. That is precisely the class you commissioned the sweep for, and the sweep found it. One test closes it.

I also want to be straight about the sweep's completeness: "regex:" is the ONLY string-literal comparison in the entire four-file cluster, and I checked every other predicate, comparison, threshold and arithmetic site individually. I do not expect further instances of this class here. B-008 and B-009 are the residue, and both are low-realism enough that I raised them as optional rather than blocking.

Recommendation: land B-007 (and B-008/B-009 if you want the belt-and-braces, matching the choice made last round), then re-gate. I'd expect round 9 to pass and the sequence to move to SPEC-010, the michi output/error adapter.
</teammate-message>

verdict_summary: "Fresh fixture 86/86 pass; B-004/005/006 confirmed closed. Class sweep found B-007: the 'regex:' prefix literal's trailing colon is unpinned — starts_with(\"regex\") survives all 86 tests and silently makes parse(\"regexp\") return zero terms."

=== 1. Fresh fixture and baseline ===
Built a NEW fixture crate at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl/a82f4f80-7822-4785-a872-33c66baeee45/scratchpad/fx8 — own bare [workspace] table, edition 2024, lib.rs trimmed to error+query only, error.rs plus all four query/*.rs mirrored, crates.io substitutes for the orin-cargo-registry deps (thiserror 2, serde, serde_json, camino, ignore, regex, grep-regex). No stale fixture reused.

Result: 86 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Confirms the expected count fresh.

=== 2. B-004 / B-005 / B-006 independently re-verified as closed ===
Re-applied each documented violation separately against the fresh fixture; each was caught by exactly one test, with a clean revert to 86-pass verified after each (and lexer.rs confirmed byte-identical to the repo copy afterward):

- B-004 — read_word predicate narrowed to `ch == ' '` -> caught by `word_stops_at_every_ascii_whitespace_kind_not_just_space` (85 passed / 1 failed)
- B-005 — `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` placed on its own line with a blank-line separator above `pub struct Lexer<'a>` (the exact placement that evades the structural text-window check) -> caught by `lexer_implements_none_of_the_common_derivable_traits_pinned` (85/1)
- B-006 — a second `impl Lexer<'_> { pub fn sneaky_pos(&self) -> usize { .. } }` block using the elided-lifetime spelling -> caught by `lexer_exactly_two_public_methods_structural` (85/1)

All three fixes hold. The retry-7 round's findings are genuinely closed, not papered over.

=== 3. Class-level predicate-narrowing sweep (the main ask) ===
I manually enumerated every boolean predicate, comparison operator, arithmetic site, threshold constant, and literal comparison across lexer.rs / parser.rs / plan.rs — not just the ones already tested — and checked each against a plausible narrower/wider/off-by-one/substituted variant rather than only wholesale deletion or negation.

Confirmed genuinely pinned (spot-checked by reasoning, and by mutation where non-obvious):
- skip_whitespace's is_ascii_whitespace: narrowing to `ch == ' '` is killed by next_token_skips_leading_ascii_whitespace_unconditionally; WIDENING to Unicode `is_whitespace()` is killed by nbsp_prefixed_word_is_not_trimmed_away_and_lexer_keeps_the_nbsp. Both directions covered.
- read_word's is_ascii_whitespace: narrowing killed by the new B-004 test; widening to Unicode killed by the same NBSP test.
- read_quoted's `'"'` terminator, `'\\'` escape trigger, inner `peek() == '"'`, and the escaped-quote `pos += 1` (both +=0 and +=2 die) — all pinned by AC-006 examples 1-4.
- advance()'s `pos += ch.len_utf8()`: `+= 1` dies on the multi-byte tests (日本語 slices at a non-boundary).
- next_token's '+' / '-' / '"' dispatch chars and their 1-byte increments: pinned, the first two by explicit `assert_eq!(l.pos, 1)`.
- `pos += "regex:".len()`: 5 or 7 die on `assert_eq!(l.pos, 6)`.
- `remaining()` vs `self.input` in the prefix check: substituting self.input dies on plus_regex_prefix_degrades_to_optional_escaped_literal_foo (pos is 1 there, not 0).
- parse's `input.trim().is_empty()`: reducing to `input.is_empty()` dies on nbsp_only_input_returns_empty_vec_via_unicode_trim.
- LIMIT = 64 and the strict `>`: 63 dies on exactly_64_terms_succeeds, 65 dies on the 65-term test, `>=` dies on exactly_64; and count==100 pins that the check runs after the full loop.
- All four regex::escape sites: each assertion uses an input containing a real metacharacter ('.'), so even the ones written as a re-computed `regex::escape("a.b")` do NOT self-cancel. Verified individually.
- from_terms' three Modifier equality filters, search_patterns' chain order, and its `self.terms[i]` indexing: all pinned by the partition/order tests.
- plan.rs is_empty: the REALISTIC mis-implementation AC-018 explicitly warns about (`required.is_empty() && scored.is_empty()`) IS caught by the exclusion-only assertion.

The sweep surfaced three survivors. One is material.

=== B-007 (BLOCKER) — crates/monokl/src/query/lexer.rs:88 ===
AC-004 requires the check be against "the exact, case-sensitive 6-byte literal 'regex:'". Prior rounds pinned the case-sensitive half (REGEX:, Regex: tests) and the 6-byte half (assert_eq!(l.pos, 6)) — but never the COLON. Every test input either supplies the full "regex:" or does not begin with "regex" at all, so nothing distinguishes the real literal from a colonless variant.

Mutating `self.remaining().starts_with("regex:")` -> `starts_with("regex")` SURVIVES all 86 tests.

Measured behavioral consequence (not reasoned — I ran both):
  TRUE:    lex("regexp") = Word("regexp");  parse("regexp") = [ParsedTerm{Optional, "regexp", is_regex:false}]
  MUTANT:  lex("regexp") = RegexPrefix;     parse("regexp") = []      <-- zero terms, silently
(The increment stays 6, so "regexp" is consumed entirely, RegexPrefix is emitted, then pattern_tok is Eof and the wildcard arm drops it.) "regexes", "regexbuilder", etc. degrade identically. A user searching for "regexp" gets a silently empty result set — a real, wrong, undiagnosed search result.

Fix (I verified it: passes clean on unmutated code and kills the mutant). Add to lexer.rs's test module:

    // AC-004: the "regex:" prefix check requires the trailing colon -- a word
    // merely STARTING with "regex" is an ordinary Word. Every other regex-prefix
    // test in this file either supplies the full 6-byte literal or an input that
    // doesn't begin with "regex" at all, so none can distinguish the real literal
    // from a colonless `starts_with("regex")` variant.
    #[test]
    fn regex_prefix_requires_the_trailing_colon() {
        let mut l = Lexer::new("regexp");
        assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::Word("regexp".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(l.next_token(), Token::Eof);
        let mut l2 = Lexer::new("regex foo");
        assert_eq!(l2.next_token(), Token::Word("regex".to_string()));
        assert_eq!(l2.next_token(), Token::Word("foo".to_string()));
    }

(Optionally mirror end-to-end in parser.rs with parse("regexp") -> one Optional non-regex term with pattern "regexp".)

=== Optional hardening (your call, same as B-005/B-006 last round) ===
- B-008 — lexer.rs:50. The B-004 test covers \t \n \r but NOT form feed (0x0C), which is_ascii_whitespace() includes. A hand-rolled `matches!(ch, ' '|'\t'|'\n'|'\r')` predicate survives all 86. Fix: `word_stops_at_form_feed` on "foo\x0Cbar". Lower realism than B-007 — excluding exactly form-feed while keeping \r is not a natural code shape.
- B-009 — plan.rs:25. `is_empty()` -> `self.terms.len() <= 1` survives (tests only exercise 0-term and 2-term plans). Fix: a single-term `assert!(!qp.is_empty())`. Low realism — an off-by-one inside an is_empty is an unnatural shape.
I verified both proposed tests pass clean and kill their mutants; with all three added the suite is 89/89.

One more I judged NOT worth raising: AC-002 says Lexer carries no derive "of any kind", and the 9 trait probes cover the common std derivables but not serde. A `#[derive(Serialize)]` would still be caught by the structural window check unless ALSO placed with a blank-line separator. Implausible derive x unnatural placement — not a real gap.

=== 4. Mutation testing (cargo-mutants 27.1.0, scoped to src/query/*.rs) ===
51 mutants: 28 caught, 4 unviable, 18 timeouts, 1 missed.
- The 1 MISSED is `src/query/parser.rs:91: delete match arm Token::RegexPrefix in content_to_term`. This is provably EQUIVALENT — deleting the arm falls through to the adjacent `_ => None`, returning the same value. Not a gap. (Consistent with prior rounds.)
- The 18 timeouts are all non-terminating mutants (pos decrements/multiplications, read_word returning "" without advancing) that hang the parse loop. A hanging implementation is detected by the suite; cargo-mutants just doesn't score it as "caught".

Crucially, this run CONFIRMS the structural blind spot the retry-7 gate identified. cargo-mutants generated no mutation of the "regex:" string literal's CONTENT at all — its repertoire is guard->true, delete-arm, arithmetic-operator swap, and return-value replacement. It cannot substitute string-literal contents, which is exactly why six prior clean runs plus this seventh gave false reassurance on B-007. The manual sweep was the only thing that could have found it.

=== 5. Fresh adversarial sweep across all 22 ACs ===
Re-derived each criterion from the spec and re-checked coverage from scratch. AC-001 through AC-022 are otherwise fully and correctly pinned — including the Token exhaustive-match variant-count guarantee (parser.rs's main loop has no wildcard, so a 7th variant is a compile error), Modifier's discriminant-order assertions, the AC-019 direct-construction carve-out, AC-022's OOB panic, and AC-021's mod.rs surface. AC-010/AC-011 have minor untested-but-equivalent input variants (Minus-as-content, Plus-as-pattern_tok) that route through the same already-tested wildcard arms — adequate, not gaps. The only defective criterion is AC-004, via B-007.

=== 6. Honest assessment of B-007's nature ===
B-007 is NOT a new defect class. It is a bounded, closeable instance of the SAME class as B-003/B-004: a predicate or literal where every existing test input satisfies both the true form and a plausible variant, so the variant survives. That is precisely the class you commissioned the sweep for, and the sweep found it. One test closes it.

I also want to be straight about the sweep's completeness: "regex:" is the ONLY string-literal comparison in the entire four-file cluster, and I checked every other predicate, comparison, threshold and arithmetic site individually. I do not expect further instances of this class here. B-008 and B-009 are the residue, and both are low-realism enough that I raised them as optional rather than blocking.

Recommendation: land B-007 (and B-008/B-009 if you want the belt-and-braces, matching the choice made last round), then re-gate. I'd expect round 9 to pass and the sequence to move to SPEC-010, the michi output/error adapter.

Fresh isolated crate at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-gabe-Projects-monokl/a82f4f80-7822-4785-a872-33c66baeee45/scratchpad/fx11` — own bare `[workspace]`, edition 2024, lib.rs trimmed to `error` + `query`, crates.io deps substituted (thiserror/serde/serde_json/camino/ignore/regex/grep-regex). No stale fixture reused. All 4 query files confirmed **byte-identical** to the repo via `diff -q`, and the repo working tree is clean for `crates/monokl/src/query/` — so every finding below applies to the real code.

## Authoritative test count: 91, not 92

Counted directly by module:

| Module | Tests |
|---|---|
| `error` (pre-existing, SPEC-001) | 13 |
| `query` (mod.rs) | 3 |
| `query::lexer` | 31 |
| `query::parser` | 31 |

78 of those are query tests. The fix agent's 92 was a miscount — I reproduced exactly 92 only when I temporarily added my own probe module to the fixture. There is no regression and no missing test; 91 is correct.

## B-012 is genuinely closed

I injected each documented evasion into mod.rs individually and ran the suite each time. All 5 fail `mod_rs_exact_reexport_surface_structural`:

| # | Form | Result |
|---|---|---|
| R9-a | `pub use lexer::{Lexer, Token};` | CAUGHT |

index 82d812d..3f993bd 100644
--- a/crates/monokl/src/query/mod.rs
+++ b/crates/monokl/src/query/mod.rs
@@ -78,4 +78,49 @@ mod tests {
             "mod.rs's pre-test portion must contain exactly these 5 declarations, in this exact order, and nothing else (AC-021)"
         );
     }
+
+    // AC-021: the test above (`mod_rs_exact_reexport_surface_structural`)
+    // only scans the portion of the file BEFORE the `#[cfg(test)]` marker --
+    // it has no visibility into anything appended after `mod tests { ... }`'s
+    // closing brace. A top-level declaration placed there (e.g. `pub use
+    // lexer::Token;` at end-of-file) is ordinary, live, public Rust that
+    // creates a `query::Token` path in violation of AC-021, yet is invisible
+    // to that test. This test closes that gap by scanning the ENTIRE file
+    // for top-level (non-indented, non-comment) lines, rather than only the
+    // pre-test-module head, and asserting the complete set is exactly the
+    // same 5 declarations plus the `#[cfg(test)]` / `mod tests {` / closing
+    // `}` markers that bound this very test module.
+    //
+    // Indentation-based filtering, not brace-counting: a brace-matching
+    // approach that counts `{`/`}` characters to find and excise the `mod
+    // tests { ... }` block does NOT work here, because `include_str!` pulls
+    // in this very file, including this matcher's own `'{' => ...` /
+    // `'}' => ...` source lines -- feeding the matcher's own source back
+    // into itself corrupts the depth count (the same self-reference trap
+    // documented in lexer.rs's `lexer_struct_has_no_derive_and_private_fields_structural`
+    // test). Filtering on leading-whitespace instead sidesteps this: every
+    // line inside `mod tests { ... }` is indented except its own closing
+    // `}`, so a plain per-line check needs no brace characters in its own
+    // source at all.
+    #[test]
+    fn mod_rs_has_no_declarations_outside_the_scanned_head() {
+        let src = include_str!("mod.rs");
+        let top_level: Vec<&str> = src
+            .lines()
+            .filter(|l| !l.is_empty() && !l.starts_with(char::is_whitespace))
+            .filter(|l| !l.starts_with("//"))
+            .filter(|l| !matches!(*l, "#[cfg(test)]" | "mod tests {" | "}"))
+            .collect();
+        assert_eq!(
+            top_level,
+            vec![
+                "pub mod lexer;",
+                "pub mod parser;",
+                "pub mod plan;",
+                "pub use parser::{Modifier, ParsedTerm, parse};",
+                "pub use plan::QueryPlan;",
+            ],
+            "mod.rs must contain no top-level declaration anywhere in the file, including after the test module, beyond these 5 (AC-021)"
+        );
+    }
 }
